description: Partial research snapshot; component records retain their original evidence quality. Embedding proximity is similarity, not validated compatibility. Model revision for cached embeddings was not recorded.

games.name: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow

components.label: Discrete game modes with reset substate on transition
components.summary: GameModeUpdate dispatches logo, title, file menu, in-game, game-over, credits, intro, boss rush, soul trade and sound test handlers. Returning -1 preserves the mode, -2 increments it, and another value selects that mode; changing mode clears both update-stage fields. Debug handlers exist, but their presence does not establish normal player access.

components.label: Reset chord with one-update suppression
components.summary: The reset check accepts the full A+B+Select+Start held chord only when some new input exists and the newly pressed set is not itself the entire chord. An anonymous guard bit cancels one check and clears itself. The main loop then invokes BIOS SoftReset with RESET_ALL; a generic hold-only reset detector would differ from this code.

components.label: Edge, held and repeated input with priority override
components.summary: UpdateInput forms newly pressed bits from current and previous held inputs; menu repeat waits 32 updates and repeats every 6. Gameplay has separate held/new fields that a caller can override. Despite its comment claiming larger priorities win, SetPlayerInput actually accepts a smaller numeric priority or an empty priority slot; extraction follows the branch.

components.label: Skippable timed publisher logo
components.summary: The logo handler initializes BG0, fades from brightness increase, holds for 240 updates and accepts Start/A to proceed early. It fades back out before returning the title mode. The same stage processes a Konami-code state, but its unlock consequences are not established here.

components.label: Animated title idles into story intro
components.summary: The title uses mode 1, affine BG2, object window and staged alpha/brightness animation. In its interactive state it resets a 600-update idle countdown on Up/Down repeat; expiry sets a flag that directs the exit to GAME_MODE_INTRO_CUTSCENE. Start/A can skip animation stages 2 through 7, so this is an intro replay path rather than evidence of a recorded gameplay demo.

components.label: Verified SRAM records and slot lock bits
components.summary: The SRAM initializer tests a 16-byte game signature and clears storage in 4096-byte chunks when initializing it. Save-slot writes have a 0x47C-byte stride and serialize character data, metadata and map/progress blocks. Writes lock then unlock the slot and verify each block, but this routine unlocks even after a reported write error; a slot lock is not proof of atomic durability.

components.label: Game-over presentation returns to boot logo
components.summary: GameModeGameOverUpdate builds a localized game-over presentation, runs fades and waits in stage 3 for any new input. After its exit transition it returns GAME_MODE_KONAMI_LOGO. The inspected handler does not directly reload the last save or offer a verified continue selection.

components.label: Boss-rush normalized start configuration
components.summary: The boss-rush menu clears the consumable inventory and gives the normal character one of item indices 3,4,5,6,23,24, then initializes level 40. The alternate character follows a separate initial-stat path with eight stat-boost calls. Both refill HP/MP before starting the boss-rush script; item names and the encounter sequence remain unverified.

components.label: Independent weapon, armor, accessory and soul equipment slots
components.summary: The persistent character struct stores one equipped weapon, armor and accessory plus separate red, blue and yellow soul indices, and four remappable action-button masks. Inventory storage is separate from equipped indices. This records a composable loadout shape; exact stat bonuses and every equipment-validation path are not inferred from the struct alone.

components.label: Separate fixed arrays for consumables and equipment
components.summary: The persistent state allocates 32 item entries, 59 weapon entries, 25 armor entries and 20 accessory entries. These are storage capacities rather than verified numbers of obtainable objects. Acquisition, shop prices and per-item stack limits were not recovered from the opened C routines.

components.label: Packed soul inventories with two count banks
components.summary: Red, blue and yellow soul quantities are stored in two banks, with two 4-bit counts per byte. The group-add helper clamps a selected count to 0..9; the aggregate getter sums both banks. Ability souls use a shared array rather than independent bank pointers, so the aggregate helper appears to add that array twice for type 3; no gameplay conclusion is drawn from that unresolved behavior.

components.label: Cumulative acquisition counter differs from current inventory
components.summary: SoulInventory_AddAmountToFirstGroupTotal increases a lifetime counter on positive acquisition and caps it at 999, even when the local count clamps at 9. Negative additions do not decrease this counter. The distinct AddAmountToSoulTotal helper calls the generic group adder and does not itself update this counter, so a call-site audit is required before assuming all acquisitions are counted identically.

components.label: Remove equipped soul when its total becomes zero
components.summary: sub_08032D58 checks the total for a soul type/index and clears its equipped byte if none remain. Inventory indices are zero based while equipped values are compared with index+1, leaving zero as no equipped soul. This is a concrete inventory-to-action availability dependency.

components.label: Distinct soul collection percentage
components.summary: The completion routine counts distinct nonzero totals across 55 red, 24 blue and 35 yellow indices and divides count*1000 by the combined 114. Duplicate quantities do not increase this score; ability type 3 is excluded from its loops. The raw result is tenths of a percent and not a record of player combat skill.

components.label: Red-soul cast converts MP to bounded active entities
components.summary: An independently ROM-recovered casting transaction requires Up plus newly pressed configured attack, a legal actor state, compatible active effect ownership, strictly more MP than the selected cost, capacity and a free entity. Allocation failure consumes no MP. Successful casts publish an entity slot and metadata; some ability modes zero movement and enter a cast pose with timer32. The versioned IR package emits a294-byte native component with explicit allocator, animation and effect-lifecycle dependencies; it is not yet an integrated projectile system. A separate qualified ability.package.json now supplies the native casting adapter and independently recovered starter-bone/contact-partner lifecycle; other ability callbacks remain retained original implementations.
writes: effects.active_type when count0 even if a later check rejects cast
actor.cast_state, velocity and acceleration for locked cast modes

components.label: Defense subtraction, resistance and minimum incoming damage
components.summary: For the ordinary flag branch, sub_08021654 computes floor((4*attack-2*DEF)/2), or shifts by two instead when a matching resistance mask applies; status bit 4 then doubles this value, followed by a minimum of 1. A boss-rush flag switches to a separate expression involving attack, an anonymous runtime stat and maxHP. Invulnerability state returns early; lethal HP loss sets a death flag and state 7. Parameter names for anonymous masks remain provisional.

components.label: Armor-specific random damage negation
components.summary: After computing damage, the incoming-damage routine checks equippedArmor == 23 and a low-nibble RNG result below four; success gives zero-damage feedback and returns before HP loss. Four of the sixteen possible nibble outcomes satisfy the predicate. Interpreting this as a 25% chance assumes the relevant RNG nibble is uniform; that distribution was not measured.

components.label: Health gains saturate at maximum
components.summary: sub_08021FEC adds an amount to currentHP, clips values above maxHP and emits recovery feedback. The health field is signed 16-bit while its maximum is unsigned 16-bit. Lower-bound handling belongs to damage paths; this helper alone does not prove all callers pass positive healing amounts.

components.label: Magic gains and drains use asymmetric clamps
components.summary: The MP-add helper changes a zero requested addition to one, adds it and clamps above maxMP; the drain helper subtracts and clamps below zero. Red-soul casting deducts its own checked cost rather than calling this drain helper. Regeneration rate, guardian-soul continuous drain and consumable effects were not established in the opened code.

components.label: Cubic experience thresholds and banded stat growth
components.summary: Level-up repeats while experience reaches the threshold for currentLevel+1, stopping at level 99. The threshold helper is n*(n+1)*(3*n+8); each step adds 12 maxHP and uses currentLevel//5 to choose MP and stat increments. Intelligence uses the growth table except every fourth current level, which adds one; luck adds one per step. Exact XP award sources and any full refill on level-up are not established by this routine.

components.label: Different base-stat configurations for two character branches
components.summary: Initialization sets level 1 and selects by currentCharacter == 0. The normal branch starts with maxHP 320, maxMP 80 and STR/CON/INT/LCK 10/12/11/9; the other starts 800/500 and 15/12/10/20. Struct comments identify these as Soma and Julius, but unlocking the alternate character was not independently traced.

components.label: Empty character state initializes starting room and equipment
components.summary: sub_08014548 runs its bootstrap only when level is zero: it clears equipped souls, grants weapon and armor entry zero, initializes statistics, refills HP/MP and chooses area 0 room 0. Several setup calls remain anonymous, so their named equipment and broader starting-route consequences are not invented.

components.label: Exploration percentage from discovered map-cell bits
components.summary: sub_08011E24 scans a 64 by 40 bitmap and returns discovered_count*1000/848 using integer division. A companion display routine renders the result as percent with one decimal. This establishes an exploration metric and a denominator, not that every bitmap cell is reachable or that a full traversal was observed.

components.label: Room graph encoded in map-cell area and room fields
components.summary: CheckRoomTransition adds offsets shifted by eight to roomMapXPos/YPos, indexes a 64-column map and decodes area from bits 6..9 and room from bits 0..5. It then compares the room pointer to a sentinel-terminated transition-room list. This supplies an authored room-navigation substrate; the actual ability-gate graph has not been extracted.

components.label: Entity and camera fixed-point coordinate conversion
components.summary: The room-coordinate helpers add background-1 camera coordinates to entity screen coordinates. CameraPart exposes a 16-bit fraction and 16-bit integer; entity position helpers use the upper 16 bits of the corresponding 32-bit field. This is coordinate representation evidence, not an extracted player acceleration, gravity or jump model.

components.label: Bounded callback-driven entity allocation
components.summary: EntityCreate scans slots 0..207 and returns the first free slot, while EntityCreateInRange scans inclusive caller-supplied bounds. Both clear state and install an update function; failed allocation returns NULL. The main ordinary-entity update skips updates when unk_A074_0 is set but still traverses draw callbacks, making pause/scene gating part of the system contract.

components.label: Shifted recurrence with alternate RNG stream
components.summary: The primary generator updates a u32 state by (state>>8)*0x3243F6AD+0x1B0CB175. RandomNumberGenerator2 uses that primary recurrence normally, but an anonymous mode flag switches to a second state multiplied without the eight-bit shift. These are two distinct sequences; the source alone does not establish random-quality or calibrated event probabilities.

components.label: Mask-sampled temporary background shake
components.summary: sub_08011CD0 samples RNG values masked by configured horizontal/vertical masks while a duration counter is active, then clears offsets and masks on expiry. AgbMain temporarily adds these offsets to BG1..BG3 register shadows around hardware transfer and subtracts them afterwards. Pausing via unk_A074_0 stops the shake update; this is a screen effect rather than a recovered camera-follow policy.

components.label: Deferred wrapping tilemap writes
components.summary: BgCmdBuffer_TransferToVram consumes queued background commands and writes tilemap entries with horizontal/vertical wrapping based on 32- or 64-tile dimensions. The inspected transfer body implements BG0/BG1 and resets the command pointer afterwards. String/number writers construct tile entries, so the queue is shared by interface presentation and tile backgrounds.

components.label: Tile-font strings and fixed-width numbers
components.summary: BgCmdBuffer_WriteString encodes characters into BG0 tile entries with palette selection, and BgCmdBuffer_WriteNumber formats a bounded-width signed number into queued entries. Buffer-capacity checks return NULL when there is insufficient room. This is verified interface-rendering infrastructure; a full gameplay HUD layout was not observed in the capture.

components.label: Direct and indirect queued DMA3 uploads
components.summary: The DMA queue supports embedded-data uploads and pointer-based uploads, aligns the next entry to four bytes and runs transfers on DMA3. Queue-add helpers check capacity and can return NULL; the direct-copy helper also rejects a zero byte count. AgbMain processes the queue before background commands and final display-control write.

components.label: Double-buffered per-scanline scroll distortion
components.summary: HBlankEffectSetup configures write size, destination and stop line; AgbMain swaps the filled buffer on request, preloads its first entry and VblankInterrupt arms repeating HBlank DMA0. Captures observed HBlank writes to BG1 horizontal/vertical scroll registers over 1308 frames with at least 32 active scanlines. The opened effect helper generates sinusoidal horizontal scroll over a selected scanline range; not all possible effects were observed.

components.label: Per-line hardware-window circle
components.summary: sub_08002324 computes horizontal circle bounds for each clipped scanline using a square root, clamps them to screen width and fills the inactive HBlank buffer. sub_08002400 configures WIN1H writes across 160 entries. This is source-confirmed capability; the baseline capture reported zero window-group raster frames, so its use was not observed in that run.

components.label: Mode-1 affine title with blending and object window
components.summary: The title handler explicitly enables mode 1, BG2, sprites and object-window clipping and repeatedly updates affine-title state while modulating alpha and brightness. Across both phases, telemetry recorded 1718 mode-1 frames and otherwise mode 0; this is not evidence for mode-1 gameplay. The title image visibly contains a moon/eclipse and animated logo.

components.label: Side-view orthographic scene staging
components.summary: Inspected courtyard keyframes show characters on one horizontal ground line in front of layered stone architecture, rendered from the side. The room coordinate helpers use x/y without a separate gameplay depth coordinate. These facts support side-view scene presentation; the keyframes alone cannot distinguish interactive play from scripted story animation.

components.label: Stone courtyard and supernatural title motifs
components.summary: The inspected scene shows gray block masonry, tall sculpted statues, grass and a cool purple sky, with small colored sprite characters. The title uses a dark field, eclipse/moon motif and saturated red lettering. These are directly observed style/setting cues usable for style vocabulary; the full plot, factions, year and narrative constraints are not established here.

components.label: Authored intro rendered with game backgrounds and entities
components.summary: The separate intro handler clears entities, loads several background layers, allocates an intro entity and stages music, alpha and scrolling. The frontend capture shows a downed character and later groups of characters/enemies in the same courtyard; without input/session evidence these are treated as story scenes rather than playable segments. Dialogue script semantics and story prerequisites remain open.

components.label: MP2K sequencer with observed DirectSound-A output
components.summary: InitializeAudio starts the m4a engine, prepares eight music players with silent songs and stops them. AudioVSync runs the mixer and volume updates. Telemetry observed DirectSound A at about 10512 Hz for most frames and no DirectSound B; PSG triggers were seen but playing-frame counters remained zero, so sustained PSG output is not claimed.

components.label: Priority arbitration and stateful song-volume ramps
components.summary: StartSong starts a paused player or replaces an active track when the requested song priority is at least the current priority. MPlayVolumeSet stores target volume in sixteenth-units and MPlayVolumeUpdate steps toward it, issuing coarser hardware updates; near-silent downward targets stop the player. AudioCommand has separate mute, quiet and loud policies rather than requiring abrupt song replacement.

components.label: Enemy defeat connects combat to XP, souls and equipment discovery
components.summary: Own-ROM recovered once-only reward transaction marks the enemy defeated, applies XP and then tries a soul, item, currency or MP drop in that priority. Luck, current soul ownership, accessory and legal drop location affect the tests; exact RNG consumption is preserved. A portable C policy with a versioned retained-service host adapter builds whole native cartridges through the IR backend. Actual Zombie defeat gives1XP in original/parity and2XP under the alternate plan without C edits.

components.label: MP-costed bone projectile with moving contact partner and owned cleanup
components.summary: An independently reconstructed casting host adapter and starter-bone update create a visible ballistic bone plus a separate moving hitbox partner. Both entities consume active capacity and release exact tracked slots. Bone gravity, spin, terrain linger, hit retirement, viewport exit, allocation failure and cleanup are recovered into native C and assembled beside defeat rewards through the IR builder. Actual native casts debit MP, defeat a Zombie and return active count/slots to zero; a second plan changes wall linger32to16without editing C.

components.label: Two target-approach increments integrated into paired state
components.summary: The helper moves signed words at offsets0x60 and0x64 toward targets0x50 and0x5c using steps0x4c and0x58, clipping overshoot in the direction taken. It saves words0x00/0x04 into0x6c/0x70, then adds the updated increments to0x00/0x04. It writes sign bits at0x24 and returns whether either increment is nonzero; which actor or camera uses this apparent movement kernel is not established.

components.label: Input suppression, press/release edges and directional repeat

Downstream handlers consume these fields, but actor identity, named actions and invocation-to-frame timing remain unverified.

components.label: Job properties resolve record inheritance
components.summary: Most selectors follow an inherit byte: zero resolves locally, 255 chooses the caller fallback, and other nonzero values redirect to a different record. Selector two reads the inheritance byte itself; invalid selectors and cyclic chains are not protected by this routine.

components.label: Structured ability parameters and flag selectors
components.summary: The recovered record layout exposes name, category, MP cost, range, area, power, effect bytes and flags. Property selector nine returns an address of effect bytes, while selectors eleven through thirty-one return individual flag bits; effect semantics and actual resource consumption belong to unresolved callers.

components.label: Equipment grants available ability indices
components.summary: Item property eighteen selects a linked ability set whose job/index pairs are scanned. A pair matching unit byte seven marks that ability state available; a nonmatching pair with job255 writes the special slot at offset0x3D, without proving that this is a global ability ID.

components.label: Mastery compares progress against per-ability requirements
components.summary: The job exposes an inclusive ability-index range through properties37 and38. Each entry with a nonzero category must have low-seven-bit progress at least its requirement; the availability high bit does not satisfy mastery.

components.label: Equipment replacement checks unmastered selected ability loss
components.summary: Inspection temporarily removes the old item, then checks abilities that remain unmastered and are not supplied by other equipment. It records flags for three selected slots, restores the actual equipment and validates the proposed five-item set; this is a preview transaction rather than immediate equipment commitment.

components.label: Equipment category masks with explicit group exceptions
components.summary: The rule uses job properties to choose an equipment category mask and reads the item category. Category22 is restricted to group4; categories23 and25 also apply group4 restrictions to item IDs311,316 and287, without resolving those IDs into names here.

components.label: Ability range enables a job-related persistent flag
components.summary: The routine selects a candidate job interval from a unit field, then finds the first job whose inclusive ability range contains the supplied index. It sets game flag job+3, unless either of two unit exclusion bits is set; this does not recover every job availability prerequisite.

components.label: Conditional paired ability state copy
components.summary: For units whose field3 equals four, indices26 and33 mirror the full state byte when synchronization is requested. Other field values and ability indices leave state unchanged; copying the full byte includes both availability and low-bit progress.

components.label: Two opposing status counters cancel each other
components.summary: Setting the two quantities subtracts the lesser from the greater and stores only the residual side. Flag bits0x20 and0x40 at unit offset0xEA track whether counters0xDA and0xDB are nonzero; their named gameplay effects are intentionally unresolved.

components.label: Duration decrement with an indefinite sentinel
components.summary: Ticking checks the first opposing state before the second, reduces a nonzero ordinary counter by one and clears the corresponding flag at zero. A high-bit sentinel returns without decrement; the function call cadence is not known, so these units are not labelled turns or frames.

components.label: Packed global flags and buffered save counterpart
components.summary: World-related flags are packed by byte index flag/8 and mask1<<(flag&7). The alternate-buffer helper accesses the same bit organization at save-buffer offset0x1F70; flag meaning, allocation extent and durable write protocol remain unextracted.

components.label: Selected item modifiers incorporate save bytes
components.summary: When save byte13 is zero, properties10 through13 apply selected save adjustments to item IDs51,302,148 and286, then use an unsigned upper clamp. The item modifiers are signed bytes, so the exact promotion and clamp behavior is retained rather than redescribed as a generic stat buff; which combat stats these fields represent is not established here.

components.label: Conditional percentage amount with lower floor
components.summary: An item property bit enables a table-selected percentage reduction, with another adjustment adding ten reduction units. The amount is floored by a record field and a final zero result becomes one; without caller evidence this numeric amount is not asserted to be a purchase price, resale value or reward count.

components.label: Deterministic fifteen-bit LCG output
components.summary: A shared 32-bit state advances by a multiply-add recurrence and returns bits16 through30. Explicit state setter and state-address functions make deterministic replay possible, but this extraction does not assert which item, combat or AI outcomes consume the stream.

components.label: Per-scanline palette updates
components.summary: The retained capture recorded derived.hblank_dma_targets ch2->0x05000000; derived.raster_frames.palette=4683 frames with >=32 lines. This identifies the destination and affected-line coverage, without attributing the effect to a specific combat mechanic or claiming the complete coefficient schedule is recovered.

components.label: Per-scanline blend coefficient updates
components.summary: The retained capture recorded derived.hblank_dma_targets ch0->0x04000052; derived.raster_frames.blend=162 frames with >=32 lines. This identifies the destination and affected-line coverage, without attributing the effect to a specific combat mechanic or claiming the complete coefficient schedule is recovered.

components.label: Per-scanline display-control updates
components.summary: The retained capture recorded derived.hblank_dma_targets ch3->0x04000000; derived.raster_frames.dispcnt_bgcnt=243 frames with >=32 lines. This identifies the destination and affected-line coverage, without attributing the effect to a specific combat mechanic or claiming the complete coefficient schedule is recovered.

components.label: Tile mode zero throughout retained capture
components.summary: The capture mode histogram records mode zero for all9000 frames, with up to124 visible sprites and seven affine sprites. This bounds the observed intro/front-end renderer; it does not establish that every later battle and cinematic uses the same effects.

components.label: Captured PCM A and PSG activity
components.summary: The retained capture records DirectSound A on8500 frames, no B frames and a predominant15768 Hz timer-derived rate. All PSG channels triggered but only channels two and three had nonzero playing-frame counts, distinguishing triggers from sustained activity.

components.label: Portrait-bearing speech balloons in an in-engine scene
components.summary: The directly inspected frame shows a portrait and speech balloon over a snowy town scene occupied by multiple characters. This grounds the presentation mechanism, while full dialogue scripts, emotion triggers and the game-wide plot were not read.

components.label: Oblique tile-like town presentation
components.summary: The directly inspected scene depicts a building whose two visible faces and oblique ground axes convey depth, with upright sprite characters. No movement range, height traversal, camera rotation or tactical targeting rules can be inferred solely from this intro image.

components.label: Snow-covered schoolyard-like settlement
components.summary: The viewed images show snow, a brick building, piled snow and bundled humanoid characters. The schoolyard-like reading is visual inference; no named location, faction or narrative event is assigned from model recall.

components.label: Partitioned inventory with byte arithmetic before count cap
components.summary: Addition searches the item partition for an existing item, then an empty slot, and rejects zero item/quantity or no available slot. The quantity addition wraps in the native byte before a99 cap is applied; this differs from saturating an unbounded sum. Removal reduces the count to zero when exhausted but leaves the item ID stored, so an empty count is not itself an empty slot. Caller limits on quantities and valid IDs remain unresolved.
writes: inventory.entries[].item_id:u16 (only assigning an empty slot on add)
return:i32 (0, failure-1, or native signed-byte excess)

games.name: Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories

components.label: Mode manager with deferred mode switch, boot repair and soft reset
components.summary: AgbMain runs UpdateKeyState then ModeUpdate once per VBlank. Every screen (copyright, title, field map, battle, deck menu, event, movie, staff roll, link battle, Pooh minigame, ...) is a Mode struct {name, init, update, exit}; ModeRequest queues the next mode, which starts after the current one exits, optionally with a heap reset. The first mode is the copyright screen, which also checks and repairs every save block before handing on. A+B+Select+Start (Start or Select newly pressed) soft-resets unless SYSTEM_FLAG_NO_SOFT_RESET is set (link play sets it); the movie player polls the same combo itself.

components.label: Affine-zoom title with context-sensitive menu and no attract demo
components.summary: The title fades in, then zooms its BG2 logo plate over 100 frames by easing the affine scale and centre (different target X when the Riku title flag is set), white-fades, cross-fades the background in 16 alpha steps and slides in the logo/character sprites. A or Start skips the intro. PRESS START opens a menu whose default entry is chosen from save state: Resume (suspend save present), Continue (a file is valid), New Game; Reverse/Rebirth (Riku) entries appear after a Sora clear, and Link Battle opens the cable versus mode. There is no idle timeout or demo: the capture sits on PRESS START from frame ~1000 to 3600.

evidence.ref: capture:attract:frames 608-952 DISPCNT mode 1, BG2 affine pa 0x100->0x15A, then BLDCNT alpha 0x1E41/0x0510

components.label: Mirrored SRAM blocks, suspend save and save rooms
components.summary: Battery SRAM holds a header, a "system" suspend block, two large Sora files and two small Riku files, each block stored twice with a signature and 16-bit checksum. At boot each block is checked; if one copy is bad and the other good, the good copy is rewritten over the bad one. The title's Resume loads the suspend block and immediately clears it (one-shot quick save). Regular saves happen at save points in field rooms, which also restore HP. The card collection (up to 999 cards) and 3 decks are persisted.

components.label: Mode-3 bitmap FMV player with IWRAM codecs and ADPCM audio stream
components.summary: Five pre-rendered movies (opening, 6F goal, 12F, Sora ending, Riku ending) play in a dedicated mode. Each movie header gives width (multiple of 8, at most 288), height, float frame rate, frame count and audio format; hand-written ARM key-frame and delta-frame decoders are copied to IWRAM and patched for the frame width, frames decode into an EWRAM buffer and are blitted to the Mode-3 framebuffer. Audio is IMA-style ADPCM (89-step table) or PCM16 streamed through DirectSound FIFOs with a timer-driven SndStream. Two subtitle lines are drawn with OBJ text and alpha-faded per language.

evidence.ref: khcom:asm/movie_codec.s (hand-written ARM decoder with row-patch macros)

components.label: Mode-0 four-layer field renderer with alpha overlay
components.summary: Field rooms run in Mode 0: BG3 and BG2 (priority 3) carry the room floor/backdrop, BG1 (priority 1) the raised/occluding layer, BG0 (priority 0, palette bank 14) an overlay layer (the debug field mode sets alpha 6/16 over 10/16). Characters, doors, enemies and props are OBJ sprites; tile animations run as a map task.

components.label: Affine battle floor (Mode 2) and Mode-1 boss arenas
components.summary: Regular and humanoid battles use Mode 2: BG3 holds a per-world arena map with wrap-around, scrolled, zoomed and (during shakes) rotated through BgAffineSet each frame; BG2 (also affine, no wrap) carries overlays. Boss battles switch to Mode 1 with BG0/BG1 text layers for boss parts or backgrounds and affine BG2 on top. Each of 13 world battle stages loads its own tiles/palette/map.

components.label: Battle camera biased toward arena centre with capped easing, zoom and shake-rotation
components.summary: The battle camera target is the midpoint between the player and a fixed arena point, clamped to stay within 48 px of the player, raised by the player's height. Each frame the camera moves 1/8 of the remaining distance, capped at 4 px/frame, then is clamped to the arena bounds (top bound 144 px, bottom extended 32 px). Scripted zooms ease scale and position by half-steps over N frames and tighten the bounds. A 32-step shake pattern also rotates the affine floor slightly.

components.label: MP2K (m4a) sequencer at 15768 Hz plus streamed PCM paths
components.summary: Music and SFX use Nintendo's m4a/MP2K engine (hand-written m4a_1.s SoundMain/ply_* commands, C m4a2.c) initialised at 15768 Hz, 8 PCM channels, master volume 14, 8-bit DAC. Battle BGM is chosen per battle type (world boss, Organization, Riku, final boss); events schedule sound cues by frame. Separately, the staff roll streams a block-compressed vocal track at 21024 Hz via a dedicated VBlank handler and Timer/DMA, and movies stream their own audio (see fmv_movie_player).

evidence.ref: khcom:config/handwritten.txt (SoundMain, ply_* listed as hand-written asm)

components.label: Keyframed in-engine events with portrait dialogue
components.summary: Story beats are data-driven events (~197 event scripts named by floor/world, e.g. 1F entrance, per-world e0..e3, boss, end; Riku B12F..B1F). Each event bundles a camera keyframe track (frame, x, y, follow target, shake flags), per-character keyframe tracks (anim, frame, x/y/z position, callback), timed sound cues and a message script whose entries pick a speaker portrait and expression, window position, per-character text delay, yes/no prompts and silhouette/focus flags. Events run in the field engine; five beats escalate to FMV.

evidence.ref: khcom:src/evt/events/008_1f_battle_guardarmor.inc (camera shake keyframes, sound cues, chara tracks)

components.label: Jiminy's journal (codex of characters, enemies, cards and records)
components.summary: A menu mode lists unlocked journal entries in scrollable categories with hidden rows for entries not yet met, detail pages and numeric records; it complements the card catalog. It is a reference codex, not a quest log.

evidence.ref: Jiminy's Journal catalogues characters, enemies and story recaps in KH games

components.label: Staff roll with streamed vocal theme
components.summary: After the final battle the staff-roll mode scrolls credits text with character, scene and logo panels while a block-compressed PCM song streams at 21024 Hz from a dedicated VBlank handler; Sora and Riku endings each roll credits.

components.label: Real-time action battle where every action is a card play from a cycling deck
components.summary: Contact with a field enemy loads a separate battle mode on a small 2.5D arena. The player moves, jumps and dodges freely in real time, but every attack, spell, item, summon or friend is a card: L/R cycle through the hand (a ring of the deck's remaining cards), A plays the selected card, L+R stocks it for a sleight. Played cards are consumed until the deck is reloaded. Enemies play their own cards; any play can be cancelled by a higher (or 0) card - the card break. Waves of enemies arrive until the formation is exhausted; battle ends on win, escape or death.

components.label: Valued cards (0-9) in CP-limited decks
components.summary: Every card has a category (attack, magic, item, enemy) plus friend/summon/gimmick flags and a value 0-9; ids are group x 10 + value (450 valued ids, then enemy and gimmick cards). Up to 3 decks of up to 99 cards are built from a 999-card collection, and a deck's total CP must not exceed the player's CP stat (starts at 275). A card's CP is base + (base div 10) x (value - 1), with value 0 priced as 10 (the most expensive); premium cards cost the flat base regardless of value but are removed from the current battle on use.

components.label: Card break - higher or zero value cancels the opponent's play
components.summary: The value of the play currently in effect (one card, or the sum of a stocked sleight) is held as activeValue. A new player play succeeds against it if its value n >= activeValue, or n == 0; otherwise the new play is the one broken. Equal values break both. The broken side's cards are discarded and the actor is staggered (12-frame global hit-stop, then break animation; enemies at least 40 frames). breakDifference = n - activeValue (capped 9; for a 0 card, min(activeValue, 9)) feeds Riku's dark points. In US/JP builds an enemy's 0 card does not auto-break; only EU applies the 0 rule to enemies. Bracer effects make a play unbreakable.

components.label: Three-card stock sleights keyed by card identity and value-sum window
components.summary: Up to 3 cards can be stocked; their values sum into one play that is hard to break. If the stocked cards match a learned sleight the result is a special move: the lookup keys on the ordered card catalog groups and count, then checks value-sum windows (e.g. three same keyblades sum 10-15 = Sliding Dash, 20-23 = Stun Impact; three attack cards sum 1-6 = Ars Arcanum, 7-9 = Ragnarok, 24-26 = Strike Raid, 0 or 27 = Zantetsuken; Fire+Fire = Fira, Mushu+Fire+Fire = Mega Flare). Using a sleight permanently removes the first stocked card from this battle unless Sleight Lock is active. 106 sleights exist.

components.label: Deck exhaustion and charge-to-reload with escalating reload time
components.summary: When every card has been used the hand shows only the reload card. Holding A on it charges a gauge (+0.1 every 2nd frame to 1.0, ~34 frames per cycle). The number of cycles needed grows with each reload in the battle (1, then 2, then 3, capped). Reloading restores used cards except sleight-consumed and premium ones. Some enemy-card effects and Mega items modify the count; Riku reloads instantly.

components.label: Three-hit keyblade combo with geometry-chosen swings and box hitboxes
components.summary: Each attack card is one swing; consecutive attack cards advance swing 1 -> 2 -> 3 (finisher). The swing set is chosen by where the lock-on target is (above, far in x, far in depth, or player airborne). The hit lands on a keyblade-dependent frame (10-20 frames, Kingdom Key 15), placing an axis-aligned box 36 px ahead (half-extents 20x12x32 px) tested against target x/y radius and z height. Hits apply per-attack hit-stop (3 frames for swings 1-2, 16 for finishers) and the finisher zooms the camera 1.5x on hit.

components.label: Attack x power damage with element affinities and multiplier effects
components.summary: Damage = attacker attack x move power (Q8.8, Kingdom Key swings 1.0/1.0/1.5x AP), optionally x a scale, minimum 1. Card value does not affect damage; it only decides breaks. No defence stat, criticals or random spread exist. Element flags on the target: guard/immune block (30 i-frames), absorb heals, resist halves, weak x1.5 (on regular enemies weakness instead stuns). Gravity deals a fraction of current HP; Stop stores damage and applies it when Stop ends. Enemy-card effects multiply (Back Attack x2, Berserk x2 below 25% HP, Element Boost x1.5, Protect/Shell x0.5).

components.label: Timed status ailments (stun, stop, confuse, terror, bind, gravity squash)
components.summary: Hits can apply statuses tracked by a per-actor badstatus task. Stun 240 frames (360 when warped), shortened by 1 frame per button press when the player is stunned; Confuse 300 frames swaps L/R and U/D input; Terror 300 frames makes enemies flee at double speed; Bind 600 frames stops movement and dodging; Stop lasts power x 15/64 frames and banks damage. Gravity squashes the sprite and holds the enemy 44 frames. Bosses are immune to stop, gravity, terror, warp, confuse and bind.

components.label: Enemy (Heartless) cards as timed passive modifiers
components.summary: Defeated enemies rarely drop enemy cards; played in battle, an enemy card grants one of 55 effects (Dash, Bracers, Sleight Lock, damage multipliers, Draw pickup radius, Quick Recovery, Second Chance, etc.) that replaces any current effect and lasts a fixed number of reloads (Dash: card uses). They cannot be stocked and are consumed on use. Bosses drop their enemy card as fixed rewards.

components.label: Friend cards dropped mid-battle and summon cards
components.summary: Each non-lethal hit on an enemy has a 1/8 chance to spawn a friend card pickup (3/4 the current world's ally if unlocked, else Donald or Goofy; value 0-8; at most one on the field, at most 5 per battle; lasts 360 frames). Picked-up friend cards enter the hand; playing one calls the ally for a scripted attack (e.g. Goofy charge, triple Goofy Tornado orbiting 180 frames) while Sora stays controllable. Summon cards (Simba, Genie, Bambi, Dumbo, Tinker Bell, Mushu, Cloud) take Sora off-screen while the summon acts. Friends are dismissed on card break or battle end.

components.label: Field first strike pre-damages and stuns the first wave
components.summary: Hitting a field enemy with the keyblade before contact starts the battle with a first-strike flag: every enemy of the first wave spawns having lost 25/256 (~10%) of max HP and stunned. The Strong Initiative room card raises this to 204/256 (~80%); Lasting Daze keeps the flag for all waves.

components.label: Escape by pushing against the arena edge
components.summary: In regular battles the player escapes by standing on the ground pushing into the left or right arena edge; after a 16-frame delay a gauge fills over 90 frames, then Sora runs off and the battle ends as not-won (enemies stay on the field). Unavailable in boss, humanoid, event and tutorial battles.

components.label: Battle id -> formation of enemy waves under a sprite tile budget
components.summary: The room's shape gives a battle-id range that is offset per world and indexes 147 formation lists. A formation is a list of waves; each wave places enemies at offsets around a centre halfway between the player and arena centre (mirrored 80/20 by facing). The next wave spawns 100 frames after the current one clears, only if live plus incoming enemy tiles fit the threshold (usually 256 tiles).

components.label: Riku scenario - fixed decks, dark points and dark mode
components.summary: Reverse/Rebirth (unlocked after Sora's story) gives Riku a fixed per-world deck (12 decks) plus boss enemy cards, instant reloads and no enemy-card drops. Winning card breaks adds the break difference to dark points (0-999); at 30+ he can transform into dark mode (faster walk 2.5 px/frame, Soul Eater sleights, Dark Leap behind the target), where only lost breaks count and taking hits costs 5 DP (else +1). Dark mode ends at 0 DP. Level-ups offer HP, AP or DP instead of CP/sleights.

components.label: Facing-cone automatic lock-on
components.summary: Outside card actions the game auto-selects the nearest enemy in front within 150 px horizontally, 24 px depth and 100 px height, falling back to one behind within 90 px. The target steers swing choice and some spells.

components.label: Visible field enemies, contact battles and room enemy budgets
components.summary: Rooms spawn visible Heartless symbols: after 46 frames, each frame has a 20% spawn chance while fewer than the room shape's max alive are out, the room's enemy total is not exhausted and the OBJ tile budget (256) holds, with a 30-frame cooldown. Touching one starts a battle (id drawn from the room's range); striking first sets the first-strike flag. Only winning a battle reduces the room's remaining enemies; up to 3 survivors are cached and restored afterwards; new spawns are harmless for 30 frames.

components.label: Game over rolls back the battle and offers continue
components.summary: When HP hits 0 the battle holds 140 frames, white-fades 100 frames, restores the pre-battle progression snapshot (EXP and levels earned in that battle are lost) and opens the continue screen; Continue returns to the field map, Title soft-resets.

components.label: 100 Acre Wood escort minigame with an autonomous stamina-limited companion
components.summary: A separate mode where Sora guides an autonomous Pooh whose energy gauge (0-3) drops by 1 every 1851 frames of walking; at 0 he sits and sleeps, refilling 1 after 1800 frames, and eats honey at levels 1-3. Levels are unlocked by Pooh-area cards and give prizes.

components.label: Link-cable Sora vs Riku card duel and card trade
components.summary: Two GBAs linked over multiplayer SIO at 115200 bps play a versus card battle (each player's own deck; card plays and breaks resolved symmetrically, lockstep with the main loop waiting on received frames) or trade cards. Soft reset is disabled while linked.

components.label: Oblique 2.5D battle plane (x, depth, height)
components.summary: Battle actors live in (x, y=depth, z=height, negative up). Screen x = x - view x + 120; screen y = (y + z) - view y + 80, so depth and height both map 1:1 onto screen Y. The arena is a wide, shallow strip (regular battles 304 x 66 px of ground), giving a side-on brawler view with limited depth; depth movement runs at half speed. Sprites are depth-sorted and drop shadows mark ground position.

components.label: Isometric-styled field rooms on a 32x16 px cell grid with height
components.summary: Field rooms are built from 2:1 cells (32 x 16 px) with left/right wall cell types and per-cell upper/lower heights, giving an isometric look while positions stay in screen-aligned x/y plus a height z (screen y = y + z). Diagonal movement follows the isometric axes rather than 45 degrees. Doors sit on the room edges in the four isometric directions (up-right, down-left, down-right, up-left).

components.label: Room-clamped eased follow camera on the field
components.summary: The field camera targets the player's screen point (x, y+z) offset to centre, moves 1/8 of the remaining distance per frame capped at 8 px/frame, ignores sub-0.2 px moves, and is clamped to the room's tilemap size.

components.label: Battle 8-way run with linear acceleration
components.summary: Sora accelerates 0.5 px/frame^2 to 2.4 px/frame while the d-pad is held and decelerates at the same rate; depth motion is halved. The Dash effect doubles acceleration and raises the cap to 4 px/frame. Knockback velocities decay 17/256 px/frame per frame and reverse at arena edges at half speed.

components.label: Battle jump with crouch, speed doubling and release-cut height
components.summary: B starts a 4-frame crouch (speed halved), then launches at 5.25 px/frame upward and doubles horizontal speed. Gravity is 0.258 px/frame^2; releasing B while rising adds another 0.25 px/frame^2, so height ranges ~32-56 px (27-42 frames airborne). Air control accelerates 17/256 and decelerates 38/256 px/frame^2 to 2.4 px/frame; reversing kills speed. Landing lag 7 frames, cancellable into jump or dodge. The Float effect lowers gravity to 38.

components.label: Double-tap dodge roll with invulnerability
components.summary: Double-tapping left or right within 13 frames rolls at 6.5 px/frame decaying linearly to 0 over 32 frames (~107 px) with a small hop; from frame 4 to the end the player passes through enemies and cannot be hit. Cards cannot be played until the roll ends.

components.label: Field 8-way walk with turn penalty and wall sliding
components.summary: On the field Sora accelerates 0.5 px/frame^2 to ~2.4 px/frame (Riku 3 px/frame). Turning more than ~140 degrees stops him, smaller turns halve speed; a diagonal is held if the second key was released within 4 frames. Blocked moves probe offsets to slide along walls; bumping props scales speed by 230/256; stair cells start a climb. Pressing A swings the keyblade on the field (20 px hit radius) to open doors, break objects and first-strike enemies.

components.label: Field jump onto raised cells, ledge catch and climb
components.summary: B jumps on the field (take-off 5.2 px/frame, Riku 6 px/frame; gravity 0.258 px/frame^2; release-cut like battle) with horizontal speed doubled at take-off and weak air control (+17, -38 per frame, cap 2 px/frame). Cell upper/lower heights decide what can be jumped onto; field states include ledge catch/hang/climb, stair climbing and an air attack. Full-hold apex ~55 px (Riku ~73 px).

components.label: Field Heartless wander, sight-cone detect and chase
components.summary: Field enemy symbols idle, start wandering with 1/80 odds per frame (0.5 px/frame), spot the player inside a ~+/-34 degree cone on the same ground level, then chase at up to 1.5 px/frame, re-aiming every 8 frames and giving up when sight is lost. Room cards change the policy: Looming Darkness makes them pursue at 2 px/frame, Stagnant Space divides speed by 5, Sleeping Darkness spawns them asleep. While one enemy is being struck, the others freeze; leaving the camera window despawns them.

components.label: Shared enemy task FSM with per-species tuning record
components.summary: Every battle enemy is a task (init/update/draw/release) whose update first maps battle reactions (hit, card accepted, status) to states, runs its species-specific states (ids 18+), then the shared states 0-17 (idle, hurt, defeated, walk, card-broken, hover, stunned, warped, stopped, terrified/flee, gravity squash...). An EmyDef record tunes speed, move/turn intervals (expressed as 1-in-N per-frame odds), hitstun, preferred attack offset, attack box ranges and card interval; EmyKind holds HP, height and collision radius. Walk targets are the player x +/- (offset + random range). Lunges are a shared helper parameterised by delay/active/recovery frames, attack id, distance and hop.

components.label: Enemy card play and card-break contest against the player
components.summary: Enemies also fight with cards. Each frame an idle enemy rolls 1/(cardInterval x enemyCount) and, if the player is inside its attack box ahead of it, requests a card; the play is refused while another opponent card or a break is in progress. Regular enemies own 3-card decks (bosses 10 cards, values 0-9) and pick the next card pseudo-randomly; room effects shift enemy values (+2 capped at 9, -2 floored at 1). If the player has a card set in play and the enemy value is greater or equal, the player's set is broken; equal values cancel both.

components.label: Shadow - sink, drift and lunge
components.summary: The basic Heartless walks toward a spot 64 px ahead of the player, occasionally sinks into the floor (1/200 per idle frame) and drifts intangible for 100 frames, unable to play cards, before rising (tangible from frame 30). Attacks are a 40 px lunge (31-frame windup, 18 active, 11 recovery, power 1.5x) and a 96 px jumping lunge (power 2x, hop at frame 10).

components.label: Air Soldier - hover, straight flight and dive lunge
components.summary: Fliers idle in a hover state at 32-48 px altitude with a sinusoidal bob, fly straight at a chosen target (3 px/frame, decelerating 25/256 px/frame^2, stopping within ~16 px or at the arena edge), and attack with a dive lunge from 53 px up (30-frame rise, 30-frame windup, 32 px) or a rising lunge.

components.label: Large Body - slow walker with frontal physical guard and stomp
components.summary: Heavy enemy moving at 0.3 px/frame with 80-frame hitstun and radius 25 px. Each frame it recomputes a frontal guard flag that blocks physical attacks from the front, forcing the player to hit from behind or use magic. Attacks are a 50 px hopping lunge (30/20/45 frames) and a stomp whose area attack lands at frame 63 and shakes the screen.

components.label: Guard Armor - six-part boss with distance-banded card odds
components.summary: Guard Armor is six separately damageable parts (torso, head, two hands, two feet). Its state machine uses ENTER/UPDATE/EXIT phases per state. In idle it waits 15 frames then chooses card vs walk with odds by distance band (<=60 px, <=100 px, farther: 2/3, 1/2, 1/3) inverted by an attack toggle that flips with p=2/3. On a card action it thrusts/orbits its hands when close (70%), else jumps or stomps; once all limbs are destroyed the torso alone chases, dashes and jumps.

components.label: Ursula - HP-phase-dependent card rate and range-banded attack choice
components.summary: Ursula's behaviour switches on HP thirds. Card-attempt odds rise from 1/150 to 1/120 to 1/100 per frame and attacks are chosen by player distance and airborne state (bubbles at range, thunder close or against airborne players, charge mid-range); bubble volleys grow 3/6/10 by phase. She only plays cards while no tentacle gimmick is active.

components.label: Oogie Boogie - dice roll effects and card-break-to-open cage
components.summary: Oogie sits behind a cage. Rolled dice land with one of four equally likely faces (heal Oogie, knives, disk, summon two minions). Card-breaking a die adds 180 frames to the cage-open timer; after more than two dice are broken the cage opens and Oogie can be hit while the player stands past it.

components.label: Organization/Riku opponents as virtual-input card duelists
components.summary: Humanoid bosses (Axel, Larxene, Vexen, Lexaeus, Marluxia, Riku Replica, Ansem, Leon, Cloud, Hades, Hook) run on the same deck/stock/sleight battle system as the player: the AI presses virtual keys (use, next card, stock, switch list) each frame. HumChooseCardAction acts with 1/interval odds, uses items, occasionally switches to its enemy-card list (1/60), stocks toward authored sleight patterns, and deliberately counter-breaks when the player is mid-card in reach and it holds an equal-or-higher or 0 card. Larxene acts with 1/15 odds per frame (first fight) or 1/5 (second) and upgrades thunder to a combo below 50% HP.

components.label: Floor-linear enemy stat scaling
components.summary: Regular enemy HP, attack and EXP are base stats multiplied by (floor x rate + 256)/256. Floors 1-9 use rates 25/102/384 (+9.8% HP, +40% attack, +150% EXP per floor); from floor 10 rates 51/76/640. Bosses and Organization members use fixed per-battle stats instead. Element affinities (absorb/weak/resist) are set per species.

components.label: Room synthesis - the player builds each floor's rooms by spending map cards at doors
components.summary: Each floor is a fixed graph of up to 32 rooms with 4 door links each, but room contents are not authored: striking a closed door opens a card picker, and the map card spent there creates the room behind it. The card's kind selects a room type whose shape row sets room form/size, max simultaneous enemies, total enemies, battle-id range, a room effect and prize cards; colour families are red (enemy quantity/strength/behaviour), green (battle modifiers such as first-strike strength, friend drops, magic/attack/item boosts) and blue (treasure, save/Moogle rooms, card shops). Mingling Worlds picks a random type. Rooms persist for the floor visit and are rebuilt from cards on return.

components.label: Value-threshold doors and event key doors
components.summary: A normal door accepts any non-key map card whose value is 0 or strictly greater than the current room's card value, so value chains push the player to hold a spread of high cards (0 is a wildcard). Story doors carry EventKey requirements - kind, colour, rule (at least, at most, exact, or TOTAL where several cards' values add up) and value - and the floor's key rooms need the story key cards (Key of Beginnings, Key of Guidance, Key to Truth) that are granted by events. Key to Rewards opens treasure rooms.

components.label: Tower of 13 floors, each themed by a chosen Disney/FF world card
components.summary: Progress is a climb through Castle Oblivion: each floor's world is chosen by spending a world card from a set unlocked by story events (after 1F: Agrabah, Olympus Coliseum, Wonderland, Monstro, Halloween Town; after 6F: Atlantica, Never Land, Hollow Bastion, 100 Acre Wood; then Twilight Town, Destiny Islands, Castle Oblivion). A floor plays its world's story in key-card-gated event rooms ending in a boss, then opens the exit. Enemy stats scale with floor. Riku's scenario descends 12 basement floors with fixed decks.

components.label: Level-up choice between HP, CP and sleights
components.summary: EXP orbs raise the level (next threshold grows by 3(lv+1)^2, max 99). Each level-up asks the player to pick one: +15 max HP (cap 560), +25 CP (cap 9999) or, at levels 2, 7, 12, ... 52, a new sleight (Sliding Dash first, Mega Flare last). Riku chooses HP, +1 AP at fixed levels, or +2 DP. HP is restored to max on level-up.

components.label: Battle and field map-card prizes with weighted values and caps
components.summary: Winning battles drops map cards (or, rarely, enemy cards from the last enemy once the player holds more than 4 map cards: 1/50-1/25 by species, x2.5 under enemy-card room effects). The kind is drawn from per-world tier tables and the value by weights {0:10, 1:5, 2:5, 3-6:15 each, 7:10, 8:5, 9:5}, so mid values dominate and 0/high values are scarce. Collection caps: 98 regular map cards, 89 per kind, under 9 of one exact card. With 4 or fewer map cards the drop is always a map card, so the player cannot soft-lock on doors.

components.label: EXP orbs, HP balls and Moogle points as timed pickups
components.summary: Defeated enemies burst into EXP orbs (denominations 1400/199/60/30/10/5/1, greedily split, max 3 orbs for regular enemies) that must be collected within 420 frames (blink from 360) inside a small radius (40x20x50 px, much larger with the Draw effect). On the field, smashing props yields Moogle points (4 or 10) and HP balls (5% or 3% max HP). Moogle points cap at 99999.

components.label: Moogle shop - buy random card packs, sell cards for points
components.summary: In Moogle Rooms Moogle points buy 5-card packs in 4 categories x 4 tiers (100-500 points), with values weighted {5,15,15,16,14,10,10,6,5,4} and a 10% premium chance for attack/magic cards; tiers on sale depend on the floor. Cards sell back for CP/5 x 2 points (+10 if premium). Overflowing the collection converts cards to points.

components.label: Card ring hand, reload gauge and layered HP gauges
components.summary: The battle HUD shows the hand as a ring of card faces with values at the bottom-left (cycling with L/R), the stocked cards and the reload card with its charge counter. The player HP gauge eases 3 HP/frame with a 280 HP main bar and an extension above it, and sounds a low-HP alarm at 25%; enemy gauges ease 5 HP/frame and stack coloured 560-HP layers. Start pauses battle with SFX muted and BGM halved.

components.label: Floor map screen with door requirements
components.summary: A separate all-map mode shows the floor's room grid, room names, cursor and, for visited rooms whose event is not done, the card or key requirement of each door. There is no in-field minimap.

components.label: Twin scenarios with world episodes recalled from memory
components.summary: The story is told as two sequential scenarios: Sora's 13-floor climb, where each Disney world is a memory-built episode with fixed beats (entrance, e0-e3 events, boss, end) and Organization encounters between floors, then the unlockable Riku scenario descending the basement. World episodes are self-contained and can be visited in a player-chosen order within each unlock set.

components.label: Disney and Final Fantasy crossover worlds inside a memory castle
components.summary: A fantasy crossover: Square Enix's Kingdom Hearts cast (Sora, Donald, Goofy, Riku, Organization XIII) climb Castle Oblivion, whose floors recreate Disney worlds (Agrabah, Atlantica, Olympus Coliseum, Wonderland, Monstro, Halloween Town, Never Land, 100 Acre Wood, Hollow Bastion) and original ones (Traverse Town, Twilight Town, Destiny Islands), with Final Fantasy guests (Cloud, Leon). Tone is bright adventure with a melancholic memory-loss theme.
