games.name: Metroid: Zero Mission

components.label: Top-level game-mode state machine and soft reset
components.summary: agbmain dispatches on gMainGameMode each frame: SOFT_RESET -> INTRO -> TITLE -> FILE_SELECT -> INGAME, with side modes MAP_SCREEN (pause), GAMEOVER, CUTSCENE, TOURIAN_ESCAPE, CHOZODIA_ESCAPE, CREDITS, DEMO and two galleries. Holding A+B+Start+Select triggers a soft reset unless gDisableSoftReset is set (it is set during SRAM writes). The soft-reset handler is a BLDY brightness fade-in (EU builds insert a language select). The Nintendo logo is shown by the GBA BIOS, not game code.

components.label: Skippable story intro before title
components.summary: IntroHandler fades in and runs eight stage functions in order (emergency order text, ship flying toward camera, Samus in her ship, exterminate order, view of Zebes, defeat, Mother Brain, TV-static fuzz), then hands off to the title. A, B or Start skips with a 10-frame sound/music fade.

components.label: Title screen with idle-timed attract demo using recorded input
components.summary: The title fades in, plays the title music, shows a comet fly-by then fades the logo in via BLDALPHA. After 17 s idle it starts a demo; A/Start goes to file select. DemoStart picks the first or middle demo from a frame-counter parity, loads a RAM snapshot (equipment, events) for that demo, copies run-length input (button mask + duration) from ROM, resets both frame counters (so enemy RNG is reproducible) and feeds the inputs through the real game loop. Any real button press ends the demo.

components.label: Three-slot file select with difficulty choice and unlockable extras
components.summary: File select manages three save slots (start, copy, erase, corrupted-file handling) and a difficulty pick for new files (Easy/Normal/Hard; Hard availability gated by unlock flags, see open questions). An options sub-menu holds unlockables keyed off completion flags in FileScreenOptionsUnlocked: gallery images (one bit per ending), sound test / original NES Metroid, time-attack records (password based) and a Metroid Fusion link gallery.

components.label: Save stations, redundant SRAM slots and game-over continue
components.summary: Saving happens at save-platform sprites; SramSaveFile is a multi-frame staged write (arrays, then file struct with checksum, then flush, then a duplicate copy into filesCopy) during which soft reset is disabled. Save media is 32 KiB SRAM, verified at boot by a write/increment/readback test. On death the game enters GM_GAMEOVER whose menu has two options (continue / quit); continuing reloads the last save.

components.label: Mode-0 four-layer tilemap room renderer with OBJ actors
components.summary: Gameplay uses tiled text backgrounds only (no in-game DCNT_MODE write besides the Tourian-escape cutscene): BG0 is an optional foreground/liquid/darkness overlay (512x256 or LZ77-sized), BG1 the main collision-aligned layer, BG2 a decorative mid layer (also used as Kraid's body), BG3 a 256x256-class distant backdrop at low priority. Per-room transparency codes re-order BG priorities. Samus, enemies, projectiles and the HUD are OBJ sprites; Samus graphics are streamed per frame (body/arm-cannon tile DMA).

components.label: HBlank-DMA raster effects (heat haze, gradient, power-bomb window)
components.summary: Rooms select a haze value. Haze routines are copied into RAM and fill a per-scanline buffer that DMA0 (HBlank-triggered, dest-reload) streams into a register each line: BG3HOFS (heat shimmer), BG2HOFS..BG3 (layered shimmer, 8 bytes/line), BG1HOFS..BG3 (12 bytes/line) or PALRAM color 0 (vertical backdrop gradient). The power-bomb explosion writes WIN1H per scanline to draw a growing ellipse, with BLDCNT brightness-decrease outside, white backdrop and a yellow palette tint inside.

components.label: Alpha-blended foreground/liquid layers, dark rooms and palette fades
components.summary: BG0 overlays (water, fog, darkness, foreground walls) use BLDALPHA; special clipdata trigger blocks walk the blend between 11 preset EVA/EVB pairs so a foreground wall fades out when Samus enters it. Dark rooms gate BG0 via DISPCNT. Palette-level effects include monochrome fade to black on death, smooth palette transitions, background flashes (Chozo hint, suit upgrade) and per-sprite freeze/damage palettes.

components.label: Affine BG (cutscene) and rotating/scaling OBJ
components.summary: Affine hardware is used sparingly: the Tourian-escape cutscene switches to Mode 1 and rotates/scales BG2 (PA..PD from COS/SIN and inverse scale, centered on screen); in gameplay, sprites with the rotation-scaling status get an OBJ affine matrix built from their rotation/scaling fields (e.g. tumbling, boss parts).

components.label: Scroll-region-bounded follow camera with speed-adaptive lag
components.summary: Each frame the target is Samus's position (or a lock-screen point, or the midpoint between both for boss rooms). Within the room's scroll boxes the camera centers X at half the screen and Y at 60 % of screen height, clamped to box edges; with two overlapping boxes it averages. Camera moves toward the target with per-axis velocity caps of 2 px/frame that are widened to Samus's own displacement + 1 px, so the camera never falls behind at speed but eases on teleports; ledge hang/pull-up uses a 1 px/frame slow set. Screen shake (e.g. shinespark impact, Kraid hits) offsets the BG scroll.

components.label: Per-room parallax ratios and auto-scrolling layers
components.summary: BG3 scroll is derived from the camera with a per-room code selecting none, quarter, half or full speed independently per axis (11 combinations); BG0 and BG3 can also auto-scroll (clouds, liquids) and BG2 follows its own offset (used for Kraid). Gives depth without affine hardware.

components.label: Side-view orthographic 2D with 16 px metatile grid
components.summary: Pure side view: world is a grid of 16x16 px blocks (clipdata) with slopes; there is no depth axis in gameplay. Facing-the-foreground/background poses (elevators, save, suitless back-turn) fake a z-turn with animation only.

components.label: Ground run with linear acceleration, slope scaling and skid
components.summary: Holding a direction adds a constant acceleration until a speed cap; releasing stops instantly (pose change to standing) except while speed-boosting, which enters a skid that decelerates linearly. On slopes the applied velocity is scaled down uphill (steep x0.6, slight x0.8) and clamped to 5 px/frame otherwise. Running never reverses velocity sign within a frame (clamped at 0). Physics constants are rewritten every frame from a normal or a liquid-halved set.

components.label: Fixed-impulse jump with release-to-cut variable height and asymmetric speed caps
components.summary: Pressing A sets an upward velocity chosen by equipment (normal, High Jump, suitless). Gravity subtracts a constant each frame while airborne. Releasing A while rising zeroes vertical velocity instantly (hard cut, not damped). Displacement is clamped separately from velocity: max 6 px/frame up and 4 px/frame down, so the High Jump impulse (7.25 px/frame) spends its first frames at the cap. No coyote time or jump buffer was found: jump is only read on the frame A is newly pressed in a grounded pose.

components.label: Air control, spin jump mode and spin break
components.summary: Jumping while holding left/right (or pressing A mid-air without up/down) enters a spinning pose; a neutral jump stays in an aiming pose. Airborne horizontal acceleration matches the ground value but caps lower (2 px/frame; 1.5 in morph ball). In spin, pressing the opposite direction flips facing and zeroes X velocity immediately (instant air turn); without input X decays at the air acceleration. Holding up/down without left/right, or firing, breaks the spin into a normal fall keeping Y velocity but losing X momentum. Spinning is also the carrier pose for wall jump, space jump, screw attack and pseudo-screw.

components.label: Spin-only wall jump with short contact window
components.summary: Touching a wall while spinning or screw-attacking zeroes X velocity, starts an 8-frame window and stores the away-from-wall direction. Pressing away flips facing (spin turn); pressing A inside the window while facing away, with a solid block 10 px behind on the wall side, plays a brief wall-jump start pose then relaunches with the normal jump impulse (High Jump aware; half High Jump in liquid). While facing away in the window, air acceleration drops to 1 unit so Samus drifts off the wall very slowly, easing the timing.

components.label: Space Jump re-jump with fall-speed window
components.summary: With Space Jump active and not slowed by liquid, pressing A during a spin re-applies the full jump impulse once vertical velocity has fallen to -2 px/frame or lower. There is no jump counter, so repeated timed presses give unlimited height. Screw Attack takes visual/pose priority over space-jump pose.

components.label: Speed Booster sustained-run speed mode
components.summary: With Speed Booster, a frame counter runs while ground speed is at the normal cap. At 120 frames the cap rises to 4.375 px/frame, at 140 to 5 px/frame; reaching |vx| >= 5 px/frame sets the speed-boosting flag (sound start). Boosting raises ground and air caps to 5 px/frame, makes Samus destroy speed-booster blocks and weak enemies on contact, and releasing the direction triggers a skid. Liquid (without Gravity) or dropping below the threshold cancels it. Momentum carries into jumps (vx copied on take-off).

components.label: Stored shinespark dash
components.summary: While speed-boosting, pressing down during the skid (or on landing/rolling in some poses) stores a charge for 3 s. Pressing A mid-air with a stored charge starts a 50-frame wind-up, then launches a fixed-velocity dash with gravity disabled: straight up by default, sideways if holding forward, diagonal if holding forward +up or the diagonal-aim button. The dash continues until blocked; on impact it shakes the screen and grants 48 i-frames. A ball variant (ballspark) exists in morph form. The dash destroys enemies/blocks as a speed attack.

components.label: Morph Ball form with spring jump and bomb jump
components.summary: Pressing down while crouched (or down while aiming down mid-air) morphs into a ball with a crouch-sized hitbox for tunnels; unmorphing requires head clearance. On the ground the ball uses the run constants; mid-air it caps at 1.5 px/frame and stops horizontally when no direction is held while falling. With High Jump the ball can jump (6.625 px/frame). A bomb exploding under the ball while it is grounded/rolling or falling bounces it up 5.125 px/frame (with +-1.5 px/frame sideways depending on bomb offset); because falling mid-air balls can re-bounce, chained bombs give an infinite bomb jump. No bounce in liquid or when the ball is wedged with solid above and below.

components.label: Power Grip ledge hang, aim and pull-up
components.summary: With Power Grip, holding toward a wall while not rising checks a 3-probe pattern (grabbable block at hand height, no solid above it, open air below the feet, no head obstruction, and not a non-grip clipdata tile) and snaps into a hanging pose. From the hang Samus can aim and shoot, pull up, pull forward, or pull into a morph-ball tunnel if Morph Ball is owned. Camera scroll slows during hang/pull-up.

components.label: Liquid drag (halved physics) negated by Gravity Suit
components.summary: When the hazard tile at Samus's position is water, lava or acid and Gravity Suit is off (or a Metroid is latched), the per-frame physics block switches to a slowed set: all horizontal accelerations and caps halved, gravity halved, and vertical displacement capped at 1.25 px/frame both ways. Animations slow, speed boost/space jump/bomb bounce/screw are cancelled, wall jump uses half High Jump impulse.

components.label: Stackable beam modifiers with charge shot
components.summary: Beams are bit flags (Long, Ice, Wave, Plasma, Charge) that combine rather than replace; damage comes from a lookup over the active combination (2 base up to 6 with all four; charged 8 up to 24). Wave passes walls, Plasma pierces, Long extends range (short beam lives 12 frames). Holding B charges: counter starts at 16, a release after 25 frames fires a normal shot, at 64 a charged shot (max 2 on screen, 6 for normal). Charge is suppressed while a missile weapon is armed. Status screen can toggle individual beams on/off.

components.label: Hold-to-arm missiles and super missiles with auto-switch
components.summary: Holding the arm button (R by default) swaps B from beam to the selected missile type; Select toggles missile vs super missile, with automatic fallback to whichever type still has ammo. In morph ball the same button arms power bombs. Missiles do 20, supers 100 damage; super missiles also open missile hatches instantly. Max 4 of each on screen.

components.label: Morph-ball bombs and screen-filling power bombs
components.summary: In morph ball B drops a bomb (unlimited, max 4, 8 damage, timed fuse) that damages enemies, breaks bomb blocks and launches the ball. Armed power bombs (ammo, max 1 active) create an expanding ellipse twice as wide as tall (95 % of 8x/4x the semi-minor axis in sub-px); every second frame it applies a power-bomb clipdata action to all blocks inside, revealing/destroying PB blocks, and damages every sprite in range for 50.

components.label: Ice beam freezing enemies into temporary platforms
components.summary: Ice-beam hits on freezable sprites (weakness bit) apply damage and, with a per-species 1/2^n chance from the weakness high byte, set a freeze timer; sprites immune to beam damage can still be frozen without damage. Frozen sprites stop their AI, become solid (Samus can stand on them) and flicker during the last 1.5 s before thawing. Timer decrements every other frame.

components.label: Contact damage resolution, suit mitigation, knockback and i-frames
components.summary: Enemy contact damage = species damage x collision multiplier, then x0.8 Varia, x0.7 Gravity, x0.5 both, then x0.5 Easy / x2 Hard, minimum 1. Taking damage launches Samus up (3.5 px/frame grounded, 1.75 airborne) with 2 px/frame sideways knockback and 48 invincibility frames; it clears stored shinespark and any pending shot. Some collision types hurt without knockback (8 i-frames). Energy reaching 0 starts the death pose, monochrome fade and the dying sub-mode. Enemies get a separate ~17-frame hit-flash invulnerability.

components.label: Suit-dependent environmental damage over time
components.summary: A per-frame hazard check reads the liquid/room hazard at Samus's position and drains 1 energy every N frames, where N depends on hazard and suit: no suit - strong acid every frame, lava every 3, heat/cold every 6, weak acid every 8, cold also knocks back every ~88 frames; Varia - immune to heat/cold/weak acid, lava every 5, strong acid every 2; Gravity - only strong acid, every 4. Pulsing damage sound and palette.

components.label: Movement-as-weapon (Screw Attack, speed boost, pseudo screw)
components.summary: Contact with an enemy is resolved as an attack before contact damage when Samus is screw-attacking, speed-boosting or shinesparking: enemies with the screw/speed weakness bit die outright; others still hurt Samus. A spin jump with a full charge (pseudo screw) deals (2 + number of active beams) x 4 to enemies weak to beams and spends the charge. The same states destroy screw/speed blocks in the environment. Disabled when suitless.

components.label: Suitless stealth chapter (ability loss + detection/alarm)
components.summary: After the mothership crash the suit type becomes SUITLESS: energy is set to 99, only Power Grip remains active, the weapon becomes a paralysis pistol whose charge auto-builds (112 frames), body attacks are off, and Samus can crawl. Searchlights, security lasers and alerted pirates set an 8 s alarm that changes music and spawns door pirates; pirates detect within a 10-block box with a tile line-of-sight scan that a crouching/morph-height Samus partly evades. Ends with the fully powered suit restoring and upgrading items.

components.label: Easy/Normal/Hard scaling of damage, expansions and timers
components.summary: Difficulty is a global multiplier set: contact damage x0.5 (Easy) / x2 (Hard); tank increments halved on Hard (energy +50, missile +2, super +1, PB +1); Mother Brain eye-close threshold 200/100/60; escape timers 3:00/2:00/1:00 (Tourian) and 5:00/5:00/3:00 (mothership). Easy uses a different freeze-timer routine.

components.label: Per-sprite pose state machines on a shared sprite runtime
components.summary: Every enemy/object is a sprite slot (24 max) with a species id indexing an AI function table and a stats table (health, contact damage, weakness bitmask, six drop probabilities). Each AI is a switch over a pose byte with INIT/ACTIVE pairs that fall through, plus four work bytes; multi-part enemies spawn secondary sprites synced to a parent. Common pre-checks (damage sound, freeze, power-bomb stun) run before the switch; death poses route to shared explosion/drop code.

components.label: Zoomer-style surface crawler
components.summary: Crawls along floors, walls and ceilings, rotating at convex edges and concave corners by probing the tile ahead/below; falls with gravity if its supporting surface disappears. No awareness of Samus. Yellow variant 0.5 px/frame, red 0.75 px/frame.

components.label: Skree-style proximity-triggered dive bomber
components.summary: Hangs on the ceiling until Samus is below it within 10 blocks vertically and about 2.3 blocks horizontally while on screen; then spins, picks a side toward Samus and dives along a falling-speed table with increasing sideways drift, crashing and exploding into debris projectiles on landing.

components.label: Metroid homing latch-and-drain
components.summary: Homes toward Samus's head with capped per-axis speed, bouncing off other Metroids. On contact it latches: position is synced to Samus, a grabbed flag applies the liquid slowdown to Samus, it becomes immune to projectiles and drains energy with suit-dependent sounds. Only a bomb exploding on it detaches it (random ejection speed); it can only be killed when frozen and hit with missiles (stats weakness: freezable only).

components.label: Space Pirate patrol, line-of-sight detection and alarm reinforcements
components.summary: Pirates walk, idle, turn, climb walls, wall-jump between walls, crawl through tunnels and fire lasers in forward/diagonal directions. Detection is a 10x10-block box gate followed by a tile ray scan (up to 8 tiles) at Samus's head/body rows, with crouch/morph height reducing what is checked; pirates also turn around after ~1 s if Samus stays behind them. A Chozodia alarm (8 s) puts all pirates on alert and spawns waiting pirates at doors; alarm sources are searchlights, security lasers and escape-ship pirates.

components.label: Kraid - giant background-layer boss with mouth weak point
components.summary: Kraid rises from below (BG2 offset animation), then steps left/right by moving BG2 and his sprite anchor together. His body is a background layer with sprite sub-parts (arms, nails, spikes). Projectiles hitting the belly hitbox are absorbed with debris and a small screen shake; damage only lands through the mouth part. Standing platforms are his projectile spikes. 300 HP, drops a large energy.

components.label: Mother Brain - eye-open damage window behind breakable glass
components.summary: Mother Brain sits behind a glass tank that must be broken first (glass stages); the eye then opens and is the only damageable part (missiles only). Damage dealt accumulates; once it reaches the threshold (100 on Normal = one super missile) the eye closes and becomes immune, reopening later, while a beam shooter fires. 700 HP; death sets the event, starts the escape timer. Rinka spawners and Zebetite barriers in the approach are separate sprites.

components.label: Equipment-flag ability gating (owned vs active)
components.summary: Abilities are two bitfields - beams/bombs and suit/misc (High Jump, Speed Booster, Space Jump, Screw Attack, Varia, Gravity, Morph Ball, Power Grip) - each with an owned and an active copy toggled on the status screen. Gates are checked in movement/weapon code: Morph Ball -> tunnels and bombs; Bombs -> bomb blocks and bomb jumps (IBJ); Missiles/Super/PB -> typed hatches and blocks; Speed Booster -> speed blocks and shinespark; Screw -> screw blocks; Power Grip -> ledges; High Jump -> taller jumps and ball jump; Varia and Gravity -> heat/lava/liquid traversal; Space Jump -> unlimited height. Areas are revisited as new abilities arrive.

components.label: Typed hatches, event-locked doors and breakable block locks
components.summary: Hatches have types with an allowed-damage mask: normal (any weapon), missile (missile or super; super opens instantly), super missile, power bomb, locked (event/boss), navigation-locked. Room entry checks a per-area hatch-lock event table (lock before/after an event, optionally unlockable when enemies die); boss rooms lock with a timer and play an unlock sound. Breakable blocks mirror the scheme: shot, bomb, missile, super, power bomb, speed booster, screw, crumble and bomb-chain types, each reforming, not reforming in-room, or never reforming (persisted).

components.label: Chozo statue item pedestals and map hint statues
components.summary: Major upgrades sit in Chozo statue hands (item balls); grabbing one sets the owned bit and an event flag. Separate hint statues, when touched, flash the background, fade music and open the map with a target marker on the next item's location (pause flag CHOZO_HINT), setting the same "grabbed" event so the hint is one-shot. Statues also grab Samus and refill energy/missiles gradually. Some events record skipped items.

components.label: Deferred-activation "unknown items" (Plasma, Space Jump, Gravity)
components.summary: Plasma Beam, Space Jump and Gravity Suit can be collected early (owned bit set, special jingle) but stay inactive and shown as unknown until the suit type becomes FULLY_POWERED; UpdateSuitType masks them out of the active bitfield for the normal suit, and the status screen refuses to toggle them on. Collection order is therefore decoupled from usability.

components.label: Persistent event flags, boss kills and tolerated sequence breaks
components.summary: World state is 77 boolean events (statue items grabbed, abilities obtained, bosses/minibosses killed, Metroid rooms cleared, Zebetites destroyed, escapes, demo-played markers) checked by doors, sprites and cutscenes. Several flags exist specifically to tolerate out-of-order play, e.g. EVENT_SKIPPED_VARIA_SUIT is set when the Varia statue is bypassed and the suit is granted later, and map/pause code adapts to it. Movement tech (infinite bomb jump, wall jump, shinespark) makes many breaks possible.

components.label: Countdown escapes after Mother Brain and Mecha Ridley
components.summary: Killing Mother Brain or Mecha Ridley starts an on-screen MM:SS:CC countdown (Tourian 2:00 Normal, 3:00 Easy, 1:00 Hard; mothership 5:00, 3:00 Hard). Displayed seconds tick every 64 frames (like the IGT), so the real limit is ~6.7 % longer, and the timer pauses during item-pickup freezes. Reaching the exit ends the area; reaching zero is death. During the mothership escape the alarm is forced on.

components.label: Completion- and time-ranked ending images and unlocks
components.summary: At the final escape, completion % = owned abilities + tanks of each type (energy excluding the base 99); max 100. The ending image index is chosen from difficulty, completion (<= 15 % low% endings, 100 %) and in-game hours (< 2, < 4); Easy always gets image 0. The ending number unlocks a gallery bit; clear time feeds time-attack records. The in-game timer counts 64 ticks per displayed second and caps at 99:59:59.

components.label: Energy and three ammo pools with tank capacity expansions
components.summary: Four capped pools: energy (starts 99) and missile/super/power-bomb ammo (start 0). Expansion tanks are clipdata items; touching one freezes Samus for ~16.7 s during the jingle/banner, raises max and current by the difficulty increment (energy tank fully refills energy), and the first tank of an ammo type shows a tutorial banner. Totals are fixed: 12 energy, 50 missile, 15 super, 9 PB tanks. Sources are tanks, enemy drops and statue/ship refills; drains are firing and damage.

components.label: Need-aware enemy drop tables
components.summary: Each species defines probabilities (out of 1024) for no drop, small/large energy, missile, super and PB. The roll mixes sprite RNG with frame counters. If the rolled ammo type is already full the drop is substituted (e.g. full PBs -> small energy or large energy depending on whether energy is full), steering drops toward what the player lacks. Drops refill 5/20 energy, 2 missiles, 2 supers, 1 PB, and despawn after ~3.3 s.

components.label: Sprite-built HUD with energy tanks, ammo counters, minimap and low-health beep
components.summary: The HUD is drawn entirely with OBJ sprites whose digit tiles are DMA'd only when values change: energy digits plus tank boxes, missile/super/PB counters that highlight when armed, and a minimap whose tiles are rendered from explored/item data. Energy below 30 sets the low-health flag; a beep plays every 16 frames while it is set and Samus can move.

components.label: Pause map (explored + downloaded) and equipment status screen
components.summary: Start opens the pause screen: an area map combining explored tiles, map-station downloads and collected-item markers, boss icons, a world map toggle and per-area tank counts; Chozo hint targets appear here. The status screen shows a wireframe Samus with every owned item and lets the player toggle individual beams/abilities (unknown items greyed). Map stations download an area's map in an animated pause sequence. An "easy sleep" (power-save) option exists in the pause menu.

components.label: Shoulder-modifier control scheme with 5-way aiming
components.summary: A jump, B fire, R (default) arm missiles/PB, L (default) diagonal aim, Select swap missile type, Start pause; assignments live in a struct loaded from defaults. The arm cannon aims forward, diagonally up/down (L or d-pad combinations), straight up and straight down (airborne). Assignments are stored per save file.

components.label: Short in-engine cutscenes and scrolling story text
components.summary: 14 cutscenes (intro text, mothership monologue, "could I survive", Mother Brain close-up, Kraid rising, statue opening, Ridley in space/landing/spawning, entering Tourian, before Ruins Test, getting the fully powered suit, Mecha Ridley sees Samus, Samus in blue ship) run as separate game modes or in-game overlays; story-text cutscenes print Samus's first-person narration line by line. Each declares whether room music continues. In-game close-ups (Samus face) and suit-upgrade flashes play over gameplay.

components.label: Item-acquisition banners and area-name banners
components.summary: Collecting an item or tank spawns a message-banner sprite that pauses play, plays an item/tank/unknown-item jingle (inserting it before the current track) and names the item with a one-line usage hint for first tanks; area/location banners show region names on entry. Save prompts reuse the banner with a yes/no cursor.

components.label: Planet Zebes, Chozo ruins and Space Pirate mothership
components.summary: Lone bounty hunter Samus Aran infiltrates planet Zebes (Brinstar, Kraid's lair, Norfair, Ridley's lair, Tourian, Crateria) to destroy Mother Brain and the Metroids, then crash-lands without her suit at the Chozodia ruins and Space Pirate mothership. Ancient bird-like Chozo statues guide her. Area names come from code; story and tone are model knowledge: isolated, atmospheric sci-fi with a remake framing of the 1986 NES game (which is bundled as an unlock).

evidence.ref: plot, characters and tone of Metroid: Zero Mission

components.label: Custom sequenced engine mixing DirectSound samples and PSG channels
components.summary: Audio init enables both DirectSound FIFOs and the four PSG channels, copies three mixer/sound code stubs into RAM and configures the mixer through a packed sound-action word (the source comment decodes it as 13379 Hz, 7 channels, PWM 9, volume 15). Tracks are sequence data with voice groups, direct-sound samples and programmable-wave samples (sound/ directory); a DMA2 interrupt refills the FIFO. Sound effects are highly contextual (separate jump/spin/wall-jump sounds for suited, suitless and underwater states).

components.label: Room-keyed music with jingle insertion, alarm and boss tracks
components.summary: Each room entry names a track; transitions only restart music when the track changes, with alias tables so variant rooms keep continuity. Item, tank, unknown-item and fully-powered-suit jingles and the loading jingle are inserted with the current track queued to resume. Pausing lowers volume; hints and item pauses preserve channels. Boss fights switch to battle tracks (Kraid with intro) and to a boss-killed track; the Chozodia alarm plays an alarm track while stealthed; suitless items resume the Chozo ruins theme.

games.name: Metroid Fusion

components.label: Top-level game-mode state machine and soft reset
components.summary: AgbMain dispatches over 15 modes (TITLE, IN_GAME, SOFT_RESET, MAP_SCREEN, CUTSCENE, SA_X_CLOSE_UP, ERASE_SRAM_MENU, FILE_SELECT_OR_INTRO, GAME_OVER, ENDING, DIED_FROM_SR388_COLLISION, CREDITS, DEMO, plus unknown/debug). MAP_SCREEN is both the pause screen and the host for navigation conversations; the SA-X close-up is its own mode entered from in-game. Game over offers continue-from-save or soft reset. A+B+Select+Start soft-resets unless a save is in progress.

components.label: Two-stage pre-title space intro
components.summary: Before the title, IntroHandler runs two stages - a space view of the station and Samus's ship crashing through an asteroid field ("WARNING / TIME / DISTANCE" HUD). A or Start skips with a 20-frame sound/music fade. Both stage routines are still assembly.

evidence.ref: capture:attract:keyframes f001406 (station in space), f002498 (asteroid crash HUD)

components.label: New-file prologue with paged story text and X-infection mosaic
components.summary: Starting a new file runs an 11-stage prologue: SR388 preview, researchers and a Hornoad turning into an X (mosaic dissolve), the ship flight, Samus fainting and drifting into asteroids, being found and cured with the Metroid vaccine, then arriving at the BSL. Text pages advance with a prompt arrow. The final fade writes the file over four frames; completed files skip it (introPlayed).

components.label: Title screen with 20 s idle attract demos replaying recorded input
components.summary: The logo fades in by stepping BLDALPHA EVA every 5 frames; PRESS START and the copyright are semi-transparent sprites whose palette cycles every 12 frames. After 1200 idle frames a demo starts. Twelve demos (sector runs plus wall-jump, shinespark, ladder, power-bomb, Arachnus and Screw Attack showcases) play in two halves of six chosen by frame-counter parity; each loads a RAM snapshot and run-length input (256 slots), and any press ends it.

components.label: Three-slot file select with sound option, no difficulty select
components.summary: File select shows slots A/B/C with SOUND and EXIT options; an erase-SRAM menu exists as its own game mode. There is no difficulty choice in C code; completion data holds only completedGame and introPlayed. A completed file skips some late event hatch locks.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:keyframe f1528 (SAMUS DATA, A/B/C, SOUND, EXIT)

components.label: Save pads, redundant SRAM slots and game-over continue
components.summary: Saving happens on save pads (platform sinks, yes/no prompt banner). SRAM is 32 KiB holding three 4608-byte files, each with an interleaved backup copy. Saves are disabled by the event script during the power outage, the meltdown and after the orbit change. Game over offers continue (reload last save) or quit.

components.label: Mode-0 four-layer tilemap room renderer with OBJ actors
components.summary: Same engine as Zero Mission - gameplay is pure Mode 0 with four text BGs set per room by RoomEffectSetTransparency (BG0 overlay/liquid/darkness, BG1 collision layer, BG2 decoration, BG3 backdrop). Fusion adds BG0 room types for dark, dim, SA-X and Nightmare rooms. Captures saw Mode 0 in 8966/9000 frames with up to 88 OBJ visible.

evidence.ref: capture:attract+frontend:dispcnt mode 0 in 8966/9000 frames, max 88 OBJ

components.label: HBlank-DMA haze and power-bomb window with event-driven fog
components.summary: Same RAM-resident per-scanline HBlank-DMA routines as Zero Mission, with 14 haze values instead of 8 (adds BG0 haze, a cold no-op and an after-power-bomb value). Haze data also sets the room's damaging effect and water motion, and in fog rooms the haze value is chosen from the event counter (atmospheric stabilizers). The power-bomb window ellipse matches Zero Mission (BLDY 12).

components.label: Alpha-blended overlays, dark/dim rooms, colour fades and iris window transition
components.summary: BG0 overlays use BLDALPHA; dark rooms persist until the SA-X elevator cutscene ends and dim lighting follows an event table. There are 20 colour-fade types including an iris transition where window 1 grows from a point at (timer/2 + 2) px per frame per edge or closes onto Samus. No Zero-Mission-style clipdata-triggered blend fades were found in C.

components.label: Story-state room effects (fog, electrified water, meltdown, power outage)
components.summary: About 23 room effects are keyed to the event counter rather than the room alone - stabilizer fog, electrified water with a 20-frame shake, meltdown lighting between the Ice Missile download and the cooling unit fix, auxiliary power off, power outage, the SA-X elevator, reactor core and boss rooms (Yakuza, Nightmare, Omega Metroid). They swap palettes, haze and blend and fire music events, so the same room reads differently at different story points.

components.label: OBJ mosaic dissolve for X emergence and absorption
components.summary: A 45-step table ramps OBJ mosaic size 0 -> 15 -> 0. A dying infected enemy counts down 44 -> 0 through it, blinking every other frame, then becomes an X; a newly spawned X starts at index 22 and is untouchable until the index drops to 22 or below. The value is written to the MOSAIC register every frame from the in-game loop.

components.label: Affine OBJ only (no affine backgrounds)
components.summary: Unlike Zero Mission, no mode-1/2 affine background was found; rotation/scaling is OBJ-only (cutscene sprites and rotating gameplay sprites, up to 3 affine OBJ seen in captures). The ending's posing sequence uses a CPU HBlank callback instead.

components.label: Scroll-region-bounded follow camera with displacement-limited catch-up
components.summary: Same anchors as Zero Mission (120 px across, 96 px down, clamped to room scroll boxes), but each axis steps by min(distance to target, 12 px/frame, Samus displacement + 1 px) and does not move when Samus moves away from the target. Screen shake alternates every 2 frames and halves in its last 15. A 32 px look-ahead camera exists only behind a debug option; special scrolls serve the Nightmare shadow and SR388 planet.

components.label: Per-room BG3 parallax codes and auto-scrolling BG0
components.summary: BG3 scroll codes 0-10 select none, half, full or quarter (X only) speed per axis; BG0 auto-scrolls water, fog or snowflakes.

components.label: Side-view orthographic 2D with 16 px metatile grid
components.summary: Identical to Zero Mission - a 16x16 px block grid with slopes, 240x160 screen, no depth axis; facing-foreground/background poses fake a turn at save, nav and data pads.

components.label: Ground run with slower linear acceleration, slope scaling and skid
components.summary: Same run model as Zero Mission (constant acceleration to a 3 px/frame cap, instant stop on release unless speed-boosting, then a linear skid; slope scaling x0.6 steep / x0.8 slight uphill, 5 px/frame clamp otherwise), but the ground acceleration is 0.1875 instead of 0.25 px/frame^2, so top speed takes 16 frames instead of 12. Physics constants are rewritten each frame from a normal or a liquid-slowed set in SamusUpdatePhysics.

components.label: Low-gravity impulse jump with release cut and symmetric 4 px/frame displacement cap
components.summary: Pressing A in a grounded pose sets an upward velocity (5.3125 px/frame, or 6.875 with High Jump); gravity subtracts 0.1875 px/frame^2 while airborne until the stored velocity reaches -6.875 px/frame. Releasing A while rising zeroes vertical velocity (hard cut). Per-frame displacement is clamped to 4 px both up and down, so jumps are floatier than Zero Mission: lower impulse but 40% less gravity gives a higher, slower arc (70.75 px normal, 104 px High Jump). Jump is read only on a newly pressed A; there is no suit-dependent impulse.

components.label: Air control, spin jump mode and spin break
components.summary: As in Zero Mission, running jumps or a mid-air A press without up/down enter a spin; opposite input in a spin flips facing and zeroes X velocity in one frame; holding up/down without left/right, or firing, breaks the spin. Air acceleration is 0.25 px/frame^2 but the air cap is lower (1.5 px/frame, 1.25 in morph ball), so horizontal jump distance comes mostly from carried run speed. Spin is the carrier pose for wall jump, Space Jump and Screw Attack.

components.label: Spin wall jump with fixed impulse and horizontal kick
components.summary: Touching a wall while spinning/screw-attacking opens a 6-frame window; turning away mid-spin with a wall within 8 px at foot or head height opens a 10-frame window. Pressing A in the window, facing away, with a solid block 10 px behind, starts a wall jump that always uses the normal impulse (5.3125 px/frame, not High Jump) plus a 2 px/frame kick away from the wall (1.5 px/frame vertical in liquid). The same wall-jump start is reachable from a ledge hang or a wall ladder by pressing A while holding away.

components.label: Space Jump re-jump with fall-speed window
components.summary: With Space Jump and not slowed, pressing A during a spin re-applies the jump impulse (High Jump aware) once vertical velocity has fallen to -2.4375 px/frame or lower. No jump counter, so timed presses give unlimited height. Screw Attack overrides the space-jump pose when both are owned.

components.label: Speed Booster sustained-run speed mode
components.summary: With Speed Booster and not slowed, a run counter increments while |vx| >= 2 px/frame and resets below. At 120 frames the run cap rises to 4.375 px/frame, at 140 to 5 px/frame. Separately, a boosting counter runs whenever |vx| >= 5 px/frame; while it is non-zero the ground cap is 5 px/frame and the air cap 5 px/frame, Samus breaks speed blocks and weak enemies, and releasing the direction triggers a skid. Liquid without Gravity clears the counter the same frame.

components.label: Stored shinespark dash
components.summary: Holding only down during a speed-boost skid stores a 3 s charge. Pressing A mid-air with a charge plays an animation-timed wind-up, then launches a gravity-free dash (6 px/frame up by default, 6 px/frame sideways, or 5/3 px/frame diagonal). The dash ends when the relevant velocity is zeroed by collision, shaking the screen for 30 frames. Being hurt clears the charge.

components.label: Morph Ball with High-Jump ball jump and weak mid-air bomb re-bounce
components.summary: Morph Ball is entered from crouch or mid-air (down while aiming down). With High Jump the ball can jump at the normal 5.3125 px/frame impulse. A bomb under a grounded/rolling ball bounces it 4 px/frame up (43 px) with 1.25 px/frame sideways depending on bomb side, but a re-bounce while already airborne gets only 2 px/frame (~11 px), so chained infinite bomb jumps are far weaker than in Zero Mission. No bounce while slowed by liquid.

components.label: Innate ledge grab with pull-up, morph pull-in and ledge jump
components.summary: Unlike Zero Mission (Power Grip item), every airborne pose grabs ledges when holding toward a wall while not rising: the space 8 px below the feet must be air, the space 40 px above the feet clear, the wall solid at 28 px above the feet and open at 32 px (a 4 px catch window) within 8 px horizontally. From the hang: Up pulls up (a separate pull-into-morph pose exists for low gaps when Morph Ball is owned), A+forward climbs, A alone hops up at 4 px/frame, A+away wall-jumps, Down drops. A strong screen shake knocks Samus off.

components.label: Wall ladders and ceiling monkey bars
components.summary: Special movement clipdata makes wall surfaces and ceilings climbable. Holding toward a wall-ladder tile mid-air (or reaching one from a ledge hang) attaches Samus; Up/Down climb at 1 px/frame, she can turn to aim out and shoot, and after 20 frames A+away wall-jumps off. Holding Up while airborne under a ceiling-ladder tile hangs from it; left/right shimmy at 1 px/frame, shooting is allowed, A drops. Both speeds halve in liquid.

components.label: Liquid drag negated by Gravity Suit (or late SA-X suit flag)
components.summary: When the hazard at Samus's position is water, lava or acid and neither Gravity Suit nor the SA-X suit flag is set (the flag mirrors owning Ice Beam, obtained last), physics switch to a slowed set: horizontal accelerations and caps halved, gravity x2/3, vertical displacement capped at 1.5 px/frame, speed-boost counter cleared. A special slowed value (0x80) reuses the same set outside liquid (Nightmare's gravity field).

components.label: Cumulative beam upgrades with highest-beam projectile shape and charge shot
components.summary: Beams are bit flags (Charge, Wide, Plasma, Wave, Ice) that accumulate, but the fired projectile is picked by priority Wave > Plasma > Wide > Charge > Power: Wide and above fire three parallel parts (max 7 parts on screen), Plasma parts pierce, Wave parts pass walls, and Ice overrides each part's damage to 6 and adds an 8 s freeze. Holding B charges once Charge Beam is owned: release after more than 25 frames fires a normal shot, 64+ frames a charged shot; holding a charge while spinning turns the spin into a pseudo Screw Attack. Arming missiles auto-fires a ready charge. Cooldown between beam shots is 7 frames.

components.label: Hold-to-arm missiles where each missile upgrade replaces the last, with chargeable Diffusion
components.summary: Holding the arm-missiles button (R by default) highlights missiles (or Power Bombs in ball form) and B fires from one shared missile pool. The missile type is the highest owned: Diffusion > Ice > Super > Normal, damage 10/30/40/45, at most 2 on screen, 14-16 frame cooldown. Ice missiles freeze. With Diffusion, keeping missiles armed for 128 frames charges a shot that bursts into freezing flakes on impact.

components.label: Morph-ball bombs and screen-filling power bombs
components.summary: In ball form B lays a bomb (max 4) that spins 50 frames, fast-spins 30, then explodes over 16 frames for 8 damage, breaking bomb blocks and bouncing the ball. Holding the arm button in ball form selects Power Bombs (max 1 active), a 50-damage expanding ellipse that hits every weak sprite on screen, breaks PB blocks and starts a 120-frame screen shake.

components.label: Ice weapons freeze enemies into platforms; a lethal ice hit freezes at 1 HP instead of killing
components.summary: Ice Beam and Ice/Diffusion missiles set freezeTimer = 240 on freezable enemies; it decrements every other frame, so a freeze lasts 480 frames (8 s) with a warning flash in the last ~92. A freezable, not-yet-frozen enemy that takes a lethal ice-missile hit is left at 1 HP and frozen instead of destroyed; the next damaging hit kills it and releases its X. Frozen sprites are solid platforms Samus can stand on, and frozen dormant hosts cannot be revived by X. Enemies solid to projectiles are frozen without damage.

components.label: Contact damage with four suit-reduction classes, knockback and i-frames
components.summary: Enemy contact damage = species damage x collision multiplier, then scaled by the species' suit-reduction class (Varia/Gravity keep 30/10, 60/30, 80/10 or 90/80 percent), minimum 1; there is no difficulty scaling. Getting hurt launches Samus 3 px/frame up (1.5 if airborne) and 1.5 px/frame away with 48 i-frames, clears a stored shinespark and pending shot. Constant-damage grabs (Zazabi, Yakuza, Ridley claw) tick every 8-30 frames. Energy 0 starts the dying pose with a monochrome fade.

components.label: Suit-dependent hazard damage including cold before Varia
components.summary: Hazard clipdata (water, lava, acid, heat, cold, cold-with-knockback) drains 1 energy per tick. Before Varia, Samus (carrying Metroid DNA) is hurt by cold as well as heat: heat/cold tick every 10 frames, lava every 3, acid every frame, and cold-knockback rooms shove her every 87 frames. Varia removes heat/cold damage and slows lava (5) and acid (2); Gravity (or the SA-X suit flag) leaves only acid every 4 frames.

components.label: Movement-as-weapon (Screw Attack, speed boost, shinespark, pseudo screw)
components.summary: Screw Attack, shinesparking and any speed-boosting pose make Samus invulnerable to contact and instantly destroy sprites weak to speed/screw; other sprites are only stunned (SA-X boss takes 10 and still hurts Samus). The same states break matching blocks around her hitbox each frame (top corners, leading side, floor when grounded). A full charge held through a spin acts as a pseudo screw against beam-weak enemies.

components.label: Killed infected enemies release an X that is either absorbed or flies off to revive a host
components.summary: An infected enemy (spriteset class 0x20-0x4F) reaching 0 HP does not explode: it plays a 44-step mosaic flicker and re-initialises in the same slot as a floating X parasite (bosses and uninfected sprites explode normally and leave nothing). The X becomes touchable once its spawn mosaic falls to index 22, idles 60 frames, then for up to 300 frames homes on the nearest dormant host (or a room target point), finally flying off-screen. Touching it absorbs it: it shrinks into Samus over ~22 frames and refills her by colour. X ignore all projectiles; power bombs freeze X inside the blast and drag outside ones toward the centre.

components.label: Cold Blue X that drain Samus until Varia, then heal her
components.summary: Blue X hide inside solid tiles until uncovered, then drift and chase Samus within 80 px. Touching Samus without Varia drains 3 energy per shrink tick and forces a hurt pose; with Varia the same contact heals 30 energy. Any hit stuns them for 240 frames. After the post-Varia event they move to the target point for 150 frames then flee.

components.label: Mirror enemy with the player's kit - freezing ice beam, super missiles, power bombs
components.summary: The SA-X fires a three-aim ice beam (200 damage). With Varia it is ordinary damage and knockback; without Varia damage uses the power-suit column and Samus is frozen for 80 frames instead, and a lethal hit leaves her at 1 energy (unless already at 1). When Samus is frozen the SA-X follows up with a super missile (100 damage, 40-frame wind-up). In NOC it walks to a spot, morphs and lays a power bomb (20 damage).

components.label: Enemy weakness bitmask and hit-flash invulnerability
components.summary: Each enemy carries a weakness mask: charge-beam-only, beams/bombs, super missiles, missiles, power bomb, speed/screw (instant kill on contact) and freezable. A weapon that does not match turns the hit into a "solid" ricochet. Damaged enemies flash for 5, 9 or 17 frames depending on hit size, and after a contact hit a sprite ignores Samus for 15 frames.

components.label: Overshooting accelerate/decelerate homing shared by X, Core-X and Blue X
components.summary: XParasiteMove keeps a per-axis speed counter that rises by 1 per frame to a cap and moves the sprite counter >> divisor sub-px per frame; after passing the target (+-1 px) it coasts while the counter decays, then reverses, producing springy overshooting orbits rather than direct seeking. Targets are the nearest eligible dormant host (taxicab distance, alive, not frozen) or a room target point set by an invisible Target sprite, a Core-X or the lab SA-X. Some room X wait until Samus is within 10 blocks vertically and 8 horizontally.

components.label: Dormant enemy shells revived by X, plus a continual off-screen X spawner
components.summary: Enemies flagged able to absorb X spawn as dormant shells (drawn behind BG1, no collision, projectile-immune; some still twitch or hop). An X touching a shell decrements its X-to-form count (default 1); at 0 the shell plays a 44-frame mosaic and re-inits as a live infected enemy, so killing without absorbing repopulates the room. An invisible ContinualXSpawner emits an X one block beyond a random screen edge whenever a dormant host exists and fewer than 4 free X / unrevived infected sprites are present.

components.label: SA-X - event-scripted unkillable stalker with sight, hearing and door pursuit
components.summary: The SA-X is a Samus-shaped sprite with its own 20-pose state (walk, run, jump, morph, roll, shoot) and one AI file per encounter (TRO 1, NOC, ARC, lab, TRO 2, elevator, boss, Omega), each spawned only at its event. It patrols at 0.25-0.5 px/frame; on seeing Samus (10-block gate, 8-tile two-tall ray horizontal or 45 degrees, blocked by tiles, crouching/morphing behind low cover breaks sight) it either aims and shoots or runs at up to 3 px/frame. It auto-jumps 1-block steps, morphs through 1-tile gaps, and in ARC/TRO 2 turns toward Samus if she fires behind it. Chases cross doors after a 60+30 frame delay with a door-opening shot. With 64000 HP and freeze-only weakness it must be evaded, not fought; escaping advances the event counter.

components.label: Multi-form SA-X finale (SA-X, monster, ice Core-X, Omega rescue)
components.summary: On the Operations Deck the SA-X becomes a boss (350 HP, 99 contact, freeze-only weakness) that runs, spin-jumps and shoots; only charged Wave hits (9) and screw/speed contact (10, which also hurts Samus) damage it, with mosaic stages at 1/2, 2/3 and 1/6 HP. At 0 HP it kneels and becomes a monster (600 HP, charge-beam weak), which then collapses into an unabsorbable ice Core-X that flees after 180 frames. Later, during the Omega Metroid fight, a second SA-X shoots the Omega, is struck down and reverts to the X that grants Ice Beam.

components.label: Core-X - shielded ability core that must be shattered and absorbed
components.summary: Ability Core-X either descend and form their host from X (Arachnus, Zazabi; skipped if the ability is owned) or emerge from a dying host boss by mosaic (Serris, Yakuza, Nightmare, Ridley, Mega-X). The core homes on Samus inside a missile-only shell with six absorbable escort X; shell palette changes at 2/3 and 1/3 HP. Breaking the shell scatters the escorts, switches to tension music and sends the core to rest; touching it locks movement, advances the ability event, refills 400/50/10 and shows a banner.

components.label: Beam Core-X - rotating eye that opens to fire the beam it holds
components.summary: Beam abilities sit in a Core-X with an immune shell and a rotating eye that tracks Samus. The eye cycles closed -> opening -> open for 160 frames (charging cues at 110 and 60) -> fires a 3-part beam in one of 8 directions quantised from its rotation -> closes; a missile-strength hit aborts the cycle, and only missiles hurt the eye. At 0 HP the core rests and is absorbed for the beam event and a 400/50/10 refill. Hosts are a fake Chozo statue (Charge), an infected scientist (Wide), Nettori (Plasma), BOX 2 (Wave) and the SA-X monster (Ice, not absorbed).

components.label: Host-boss roster with grab, gravity-field and multi-part patterns
components.summary: Each ability boss is a distinct pattern built on the sprite runtime. Notable mechanics - Zazabi swallows Samus and drains 1 energy per 8 frames until spat out; Yakuza grabs and slams, changing phase after losing legs; Nightmare's field drags missiles down (accelerating to 0x2A sub-px/frame) and bleeds Samus's horizontal speed above 4 units by 2 per frame (reusing the liquid-slowed physics flag); Serris is a speed-boosting segmented eel; Ridley grabs with a claw; Omega Metroid is beam-only.

components.label: Per-sprite pose state machines with infection classes and X pose band
components.summary: As in Zero Mission, 24 sprite slots each run a pose-switch AI routine selected by sprite ID (primary and secondary pointer tables), with the current sprite copied in and out each frame. Fusion adds a shared pose band used by every enemy for dying/spawning-from-X (0x57-0x5A) and X poses (0x5B+), an infection class in each spriteset byte (0x10 uninfected/boss, 0x20 absorbable X, 0x30 unabsorbable, hidden flag 0x80), and per-sprite RNG from a slot-indexed table. Only pose-0 or always-active sprites update while Samus is in a sprite-stopping pose.

components.label: Hornoad - frontal-range hopper whose detection widens after being hit
components.summary: Hornoads hop toward Samus when she is within 35 px vertically and 125 px horizontally in front, and spit at closer range. Being hit on screen sets a detected flag that widens the next hop check to 85 x 175 px (one-shot, cleared after the check). Dormant husk variants skip the check and use a low-hop table while waiting for an X.

components.label: Geemer - surface crawler that curls up when Samus approaches
components.summary: Zero Mission's Zoomer crawler, plus a hide reflex - within 5 blocks the Geemer curls into a smaller +-10 px hitbox unless Samus has made no input change for over 120 frames. Weak only to charged shots.

components.label: Skree - ceiling diver that burrows and re-emerges under Samus
components.summary: Triggers when Samus is more than ~50 px below and within +-37.5 px horizontally; the dive accelerates in 2 sub-px steps up to 6 px/frame. Instead of exploding on impact (Zero Mission) it burrows, waits 60 frames and re-emerges beneath Samus if she is within +-48 px.

components.label: Zebesian - front-cone jumper and shooter
components.summary: Ground Zebesians jump when Samus is in front within 3 blocks vertically and 4 horizontally (not when she is below their feet) and shoot within 6 x 13 blocks in front, turning to shoot when she is behind; beam damage 64 (Aqua variant 55), HP 90. Wall Zebesians cling and fire. Unlike Zero Mission pirates there is no alarm.

components.label: Three countdown sequences (meltdown, lab detachment, orbit change)
components.summary: The event counter starts three countdowns - reactor meltdown 6:00, restricted-lab detachment 1:00 and the final orbit-change escape 3:00. The displayed second ticks every 64 frames, so real lengths are 23040, 3840 and 11520 frames. The timer pauses during freezes and outside normal play; failing the lab escape plays a death cutscene and failing the last one the SR388 collision ending.

components.label: Tank-completion and time-ranked ending images
components.summary: Completion percent counts only tanks (20+48+32 = 100 %). The ending image is chosen by play time (under 2 h, under 4 h, otherwise) and upgraded at 100 % (best image needs 100 % under 2 h). The in-game timer runs at 64 ticks per displayed second and caps at 99:59:59. There is no difficulty factor.

components.label: Single linear event counter driving the mission script
components.summary: All story progress is one byte, the event counter (110 events). Only event counter+1 can fire, from one of five trigger kinds: entering a listed room, crossing a trigger box, talking in a listed Navigation Room, finishing a data download, or a boss/objective callback (EventCheckAdvance requires counter == event-1). Twelve events are marked skippable so ignored nav briefings do not soft-lock. The counter selects event-based door destinations (60 rerouted connections), sprite sets, music and room effects, and disables saves/nav/recharge during the power outage, meltdown and post-orbit-change sequences.

components.label: Security-level colored hatches unlocked at sector security rooms
components.summary: Hatches are gray (level 0), blue (1), green (2), yellow (3) or red (4); any projectile opens a closed hatch whose level is <= Samus's security level. Levels are raised only at security rooms in a fixed sector (L1 Sector 2, L2 Sector 3, L3 Sector 5, L4 Sector 4), and only when the event counter is at the matching briefing event. A "no hatches" level (255) locks every hatch at game start and during the power outage, restored after Plasma Beam. Separate lockable hatches close for boss rooms and objectives.

components.label: Navigation Rooms as mandatory briefing waypoints with per-sector map download
components.summary: Twelve navigation-room locations (6 on the Main Deck, one per sector) act as story checkpoints. Using one advances the counter when the next event names that room (or "any" room), plays the matching Adam briefing, and grants that area's map bit if not owned. Navigation hatches close while in the room. Nav rooms are disabled during the power outage and after the orbit change.

components.label: Abilities restored by scripted events (data downloads and absorbed Core-X)
components.summary: Samus starts stripped of abilities. Eighteen abilities return in a fixed order, each bound to one event: six by downloading from Data Rooms (Missiles, Bombs, Super/Ice/Diffusion Missiles, Power Bombs) and twelve by absorbing a boss's Core-X (Morph Ball, Charge, High Jump, Speed Booster, Varia, Wide, Space Jump, Plasma, Gravity, Wave, Screw, Ice). When the counter hits an ability event, EventSet ORs the table's beam/weapon/suit bits into equipment; suits play a recovery effect. There is no item pickup for abilities and no toggling.

components.label: Weapon-typed destructible and reforming blocks, hidden tanks
components.summary: Breakable blocks respond to one action class: shot and bomb blocks reform after ~4.25 s, speed-booster and crumble blocks reform fast; missile, power-bomb and screw-attack blocks stay broken (some never reform across visits). Bomb-chain blocks propagate. Tanks can be hidden inside blocks and revealed by weapons. These are the main ability gates since hatches are keyed to security rather than weapons.

components.label: Main Deck hub with elevator spokes to six themed sectors
components.summary: The station is a Main Deck hub plus six sectors (SRX, TRO, PYR, AQA, ARC, NOC), each reached by an elevator from the Main Deck (11 elevator routes including Operations Deck, Habitation Deck and a Restricted-Zone link). Each sector has its own nav room, security room and tank budget; backtracking happens as new security levels and abilities open sealed parts of earlier sectors, but the event script decides which sector is next.

components.label: Energy, one missile pool and power bombs with tank expansions
components.summary: Three capped pools: energy (starts 99), missiles (one pool shared by all missile types) and power bombs. Data downloads unlock the weapon; tanks raise capacity: energy +100 (and full refill), missiles +5, power bombs +2. Totals are fixed per area: 20 energy, 48 missile and 32 power-bomb tanks. Sources are tanks, X parasites and recharge pads; drains are firing and damage.

evidence.ref: mf:src/bg_clip.c (tank pickup raises max by INCREASE_AMOUNT)

components.label: Energy, ammo and combined recharge pads
components.summary: Three pad sprites refill energy, missiles+power bombs, or all three at 10 units per frame while Samus stands on them, then lock movement for the banner. Pads are disabled during the power outage. With no enemy drop tables, pads and X parasites are the only renewable sources.

components.label: Colour-coded X refills with per-enemy odds and need-aware substitution
components.summary: X parasites are the only enemy drop. Each enemy's stats row carries yellow/green/red X weights out of 1024; a roll of 1..1024 checks red, then green, then yellow. Yellow gives +10 energy, green +2 missiles, red +500 energy/+100 missiles/+10 power bombs, and absorbed Core-X give +400/+50/+10 (all capped; ammo only once owned). Green becomes yellow when missiles are full and energy is not, and vice versa.

components.label: Sprite HUD with energy bar, single missile counter, minimap and low-health beep
components.summary: The HUD is built from OBJ - a two-part energy display, one missile counter (missile upgrades replace the type) and a power-bomb counter that appear only once owned, and a 3x3 minimap window onto a 32x32 per-area grid with a tile blinking every 8 frames. Below 30 energy a beep plays every 16 frames.

components.label: Pause map with downloaded sector maps and read-only status screen
components.summary: The pause screen scrolls the area map with the D-pad and switches screens with L/R; the map combines explored tiles with sector maps downloaded at navigation rooms and shows per-area tank counts. The status screen only displays equipment (no toggling, unlike Zero Mission). Pausing is blocked on pads, during power bombs or while dying. Most pause-screen code is still asm.

components.label: Hold-to-arm weapon button and five-way aiming
components.summary: A configurable arm button (R by default) arms missiles, or power bombs in ball form, and releases a ready charge shot when pressed; the diagonal-aim button (L by default) holds diagonal aim. Aiming covers forward, diagonal up/down, up and down. A swap-missiles assignment exists in the button table but is never read in C.

evidence.ref: default mapping R = arm weapon, L = diagonal aim (defaults set in asm)

components.label: Remote-commander briefings delivered at navigation terminals
components.summary: Standing on a navigation pad centres Samus; at animation frame 14 the terminal screen spawns and 30 frames later the pause-screen mode draws a conversation panel with portrait sounds for Adam, Samus or the Federation. There are 57 conversation IDs; the current one is chosen by the event counter (replaying the last if nothing new), 22 of them change the music, and a pending escape starts when one ends. Elevator monologues and secret conversations reuse the same text system.

components.label: Elevator monologues, SA-X close-ups and set-piece cutscenes
components.summary: Twelve cutscenes: an intro monologue, five elevator monologues that play mid-ride when event and destination room match (remind, trust, SA-X, animals, incident), Federation and ending monologues, a secret conversation, the restricted lab detaching (with a death variant) and the BSL exploding. SA-X sightings use a separate close-up game mode. The cutscene handler itself is still asm.

components.label: Message banners, room-type banners and location names
components.summary: Item banners play the jingle and hold 370 frames, objective banners 180, others 90; two banner kinds start an escape timer and switch to chase/escape music when dismissed. Doors flagged for it show one of 25 location names, and Navigation, Recharge, Save, Data and Security rooms show room-type banners.

components.label: Infested orbital research station above SR388
components.summary: The game takes place on the Biologic Space Laboratories station - a Main Deck plus six environment sectors - where X parasites from SR388 have taken over specimens and crew and an X copy of Samus (SA-X) hunts her. Samus survives thanks to a Metroid-derived vaccine, which also makes her vulnerable to cold. Tone is isolated, stalked survival under the direction of an AI commander.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:prologue keyframes ('Once the X had infested...')

components.label: MP2K-style sequenced engine at 10512 Hz with DirectSound and PSG
components.summary: InitializeAudio sets a mono 10512 Hz mixer with 6 DirectSound channels, PWM resolution 9 and volume 15; the mixer is copied to RAM and sequences use MP2K-style macros (745 sound-table entries, 661 track files). Captures confirm DirectSound A and B at 10512 Hz plus PSG channels 1, 2 and 4.

components.label: Story-event music script with SA-X chase and boss tension cues
components.summary: Besides per-room tracks, a sound-event counter (~157 entries) scripts music changes; each entry has a trigger type (room load, cutscene start/end, conversation start/end, SA-X encounter, item, security unlock, room event, elevator) and fires only when the current trigger type matches. SA-X encounters play an appearance sting then the chase theme; bosses get a tension cue first. Pausing lowers volume.

sourceReferences: https://github.com/metroidret/mf @ 55b1a54bd20c0daf5a64859850b6ebc1322bf514 (local/decomps/mf; USA target sha1 matches; README reports 3193/3607 functions decompiled, 88.5 %). Remaining asm cited as mf:asm/<file>:<symbol> covers file select, pause/status screens, nav-conversation panel, cutscene handler, intro stages and SRAM save code.
