games.name: Pokemon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team

components.label: Ground-dungeon dispatcher driven by script return codes
components.summary: After boot, GameLoop_Async runs four demo ground scripts (warning, logo, intro, title), then the main menu; New Game / Continue enter RunGameMode_Async, which alternates between the ground (town/overworld script engine) and dungeons. The ground engine returns codes selecting the friend-areas map, the world map, or a dungeon variant; the dungeon returns a result (won, lost, quicksaved, fainted awaiting rescue) that becomes the next ground start mode and picks the return script. Before most dungeons the game auto-saves.

components.label: Warning, logo, attract intro and randomised title screen
components.summary: Boot plays ground maps in sequence: health-and-safety warning (held until input in the capture), The Pokemon Company logo, an in-engine intro scene at the Pelipper post office with sprites over the BG, then the title (logo over a sunset; one of 3 backgrounds picked at random) which fades in over 32 frames. Any of A/B/Select/Start/L/R cancels a demo with a 30-frame music fade. The main menu offers New Game or Continue, Adventure Log, Friend Rescue, Trade Items, Wonder Mail and Delete Save.

evidence.ref: capture:attract:frames 0-3540 (warning screen persists for the whole idle phase)
capture:frontend:f000394 (The Pokemon Company logo), f000863-f001909 (Pelipper post office intro), f002015-f002616 (title fade-in)
capture:attract:wav rms 0 (silent while warning waits for input)

components.label: Personality quiz as character creation (nature to starter species)
components.summary: A new game opens with a questionnaire: 8 questions drawn from a pool of 55, each from a different category (13 natures x 4 plus 3 misc), each answer adding 1-4 points to one or more natures, then a gender question. The highest-scoring nature (ties broken by a random walk start) selects the player species from a 13x2 nature-gender table; the player then picks a partner from 10 starters, excluding any sharing a type with the player. The capture shows the quiz on full-screen colour-changing zigzag backdrops with Yes/No and multi-choice menus.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:f004330, f004803, f005189, f005376 (quiz questions over zigzag backdrops, Yes/No menu)

components.label: Duplicated flash save plus consumable in-dungeon quicksave
components.summary: Saves go to 128 KiB FLASH1M: the 22,484-byte main save is written twice (primary and backup, checksum and magic) with per-sector verify-and-retry. In a dungeon the player can quicksave: the 18 KiB dungeon state is serialised to sector 16 and a status record marks it present; resuming marks it consumed, so a reset after resuming without re-saving counts the outing as a defeat (all money and items lost). The game also auto-saves before entering most dungeons.

components.label: Mode-0 dungeon renderer with 24 px metatiles streamed into BG3
components.summary: Gameplay runs in video mode 0 throughout. The dungeon map is drawn on BG3 from 24x24 px metatiles (3x3 hardware tiles) of the floor's tileset, streaming edge rows/columns as the camera moves and redrawing fully on jumps over 7 px; BG0 carries text windows, the HUD row and the floor map, BG1 window backgrounds and translucent overlays, BG2 the rotate-mode grid. Pokemon are multi-part OBJ animations with terrain-dependent shadows; weather tints the palette via per-weather 256-entry colour ramps stepping 10 per channel per frame.

components.label: Per-scanline WIN0H/WIN1H via HBlank DMA for text-box shapes and darkness vision
components.summary: Every VBlank, DMA0 is armed in HBlank-repeat mode to copy a WIN0H/WIN1H pair per scanline from a double-buffered 160-line table. WIN0 shapes the text windows; WIN1 draws dungeon darkness: in dark corridors a precomputed circle around the leader (small or large by floor visibility range), in rooms a rounded rectangle matching the room bounds, with the outside dimmed via BG1 translucency (constant 8/8 alpha in dungeons). Fully lit floors skip WIN1.

components.label: Overworld (ground) maps from chunked BG data with scripted actors
components.summary: Town and cutscene maps (229 ground maps, 677 ground files) are drawn from BMA/BPC chunk data in 2x2 or 3x3 tile chunks with optional wrap-around, with up to 24 scripted actors, 16 objects and 16 effects as sprites. The capture shows the Pelipper post office intro and title screen in mode 0 with alpha blending on.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:f001013, f001223 (post office scene with sprites)

components.label: Hard-locked leader camera on the tile grid
components.summary: The dungeon camera has no easing: each frame it centres the target (normally the leader) at screen (120, 96) from its pixel position, so it moves in lockstep with the 24-frame walk interpolation. A vertical shake offset is applied for quakes; the camera may be pointed at other monsters for messages and wind warnings. Visible area is about +-6 x +-5 tiles.

components.label: Top-down (slightly oblique) tile grid
components.summary: Both dungeon and town use a top-down view with sprites drawn in a slight three-quarter perspective; dungeon logic is a pure 2D grid of 24 px tiles (56x32), entity pixel position = tile x 24 + (12, 16).

components.label: 24-frame tile-to-tile walk interpolation, fast option and dash skip
components.summary: Logic is discrete, but each tile step is animated at 1 px/frame, 24 frames per tile (12 with the Fast dungeon speed option); all monsters that moved in a turn animate together, and fast monsters that moved 2-4 tiles compress their steps into the same 24 frames. Holding B while moving dashes: the walk animation is skipped until something interesting happens.

components.label: One-row status HUD and button-chord dungeon controls
components.summary: The top BG0 row shows floor (B#F, or #F for up-stairs dungeons), level and HP with a bar up to 12 tiles (8 HP per tile); it flashes at <=25% HP and with an empty belly (belly itself is not shown). Controls: A attack/talk, L+A set move, A+B rest, B tap menu, B+dpad dash, R hold diagonal-only, R tap/Start turn in place, L+R throw set item, L+B message log, Select full-floor map. 30 s idle opens a menu.

components.label: Popup combat log, message history and explored-floor map overlay
components.summary: Every action prints to a popup log (11 px lines, closes 240 frames after the last line) stored in a 20-entry history. The floor map is drawn over the play view at 4 px per tile from visited/revealed tiles (Luminous Orb reveals all) with a blinking leader dot; Select shows it full-screen and A toggles monster dots. The in-dungeon menu holds Moves, Items, Team (tactics, IQ), Others (options, quicksave/give up, log, mission objectives) and Ground.

components.label: Cooperative-thread script VM for town, story and cutscenes
components.summary: All town scenes, story events, boot demos and boss intros run on a ground script VM: fixed 16-byte commands over 247 opcodes (messages, portraits, walking, camera pans, music, conditional jumps on script variables), executed by cooperatively scheduled actor threads synchronised by 129 locks. Dungeon boss cutscenes use separate per-boss routines.

components.label: Typewriter dialogue with emotion portraits
components.summary: Dialogue prints 1 character per frame in 3-line boxes (A/B to finish, hold B to auto-advance) beside a speaker portrait chosen from up to 13 emotion faces per species (normal, happy, pained, angry, worried, sad, crying, shouting, determined, surprised, ...).

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:f003062, f002942 (text on black), f004330 (textbox with choice menu)

components.label: Pokemon-only world plagued by natural disasters; human turned Pokemon
components.summary: The player is a human who wakes up as a Pokemon in a world populated only by Pokemon, where natural disasters are opening mystery dungeons. With a partner they form a rescue team in a town hub (Pelipper post office, Kangaskhan, Kecleon, Wigglytuff, Makuhita dojo) and take jobs; the story escalates to a falling meteor stopped with Rayquaza. Tone is warm and friendship-centred.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:f003062 ("portal that leads to the world of Pokemon"), f002792 (Charmander, Bulbasaur, Pelipper)

components.label: MP2K/m4a sequencer at 18,157 Hz with priority-overridden dungeon music
components.summary: Sound uses the standard m4a engine: 5 DirectSound channels at 18,157 Hz plus PSG, 8 players (BGM 12 tracks, fanfares, 6 SE players), 128 BGM ids, 19 fanfares, 639 sound effects. Each floor plays gDungeonMusic[bgMusic] (76 entries); boss, thief alarm, monster house and Kecleon shop songs override it in priority order with a 30-frame fade; run end plays a fail or complete jingle.

components.label: Grid-of-cells room placement for procedural dungeon floors
components.summary: Each floor is a 56x32-tile map divided into a gridSizeX x gridSizeY lattice of cells (random 2..8 x 2..7, rejected until <=6x4, else 4x4; layout presets force 4 x 2-3 for small/medium floors and invalidate the right half or quarter of the grid). AssignRooms marks roomDensity+rand(0..2) cells as rooms (or exactly |roomDensity| when negative) by shuffling a bit array with 64 random swaps; the rest become 1x1 hallway anchors. Each room is a random rectangle inside its cell with a 2-tile margin, width >=5, height >=4, odd dimensions preferred and aspect ratio clamped to 2/3..3/2. Rooms are flagged 80% for a secondary structure (when the budget allows) or for imperfections if the floor allows them.

components.label: Momentum random-walk cell connections, L-shaped hallways and connectivity repair
components.summary: From a random start cell, a walker makes floorConnectivity steps: each step keeps its heading with 50% probability, otherwise picks a random cardinal, rotating counter-clockwise off the grid border, and links the two cells. Unless the floor allows dead ends, hallway-anchor cells with exactly one link get an extra link, repeated until stable. Each link becomes a hallway from a random interior point (or the anchor tile) that runs straight to the cell boundary, jogs perpendicular, then continues, stopping early when it meets open floor. Linked rooms merge into one larger room with ~9.75% chance (two 5% rolls). EnsureConnectedGrid then links any unconnected room to a connected neighbour or deletes it; finally numExtraHallways random walks tunnel out of rooms in strides of 3-5 tiles, turning l…

components.label: Monster house, Kecleon shop, maze and secondary-structure room variants
components.summary: After connectivity, the generator may convert one eligible room (valid, connected, unmerged, no other feature) into a Kecleon shop (needs >=5x4, interior with 1-tile margin, never on rescue floors or with a monster house) or a monster house (chance per floor; skipped if a shop exists or an outlaw mission forbids it); maze rooms are rolled but a dead attempts<0 check means they never generate in vanilla. Rooms flagged for secondary structures pick one of six variants (none, maze/plus/dot, checkerboard, central pool, island with items and a warp tile, divider line) of water/lava, spending from a per-floor budget. Imperfections grow walls inward from corners.

components.label: Per-floor layout archetypes and FloorProperties parameter record
components.summary: Every floor of every dungeon is a 28-byte FloorProperties record (layout, room density, tileset, music, weather, connectivity, enemy/item/trap/buried-item densities, shop/monster-house/maze chances, dead-end flag, secondary-structure budget, extra hallways, lake density, visibility range, money cap, Kecleon shop layout). The layout byte selects a generator: standard large/medium/small grids, outer ring (6x4 with hallway border), crossroads, line, cross, beetle, outer rooms, one-room monster house, two rooms with monster house. 350 floor records ship; large (91), small (107) and medium (104) dominate.

components.label: Stairs, item, trap, enemy and player spawn placement on generated floors
components.summary: Spawns are flags on candidate tiles filtered by rule: stairs on a random open room tile that is not shop, junction, enemy or special; items itemDensity+-2 (min 1) on room tiles outside shops/monster houses; buried items in walls; monster-house items/traps 50/50 on 50-80% of its tiles (min 6, cap 7); traps rand[density/2, density) capped at 56 on item-free room tiles; enemies rand[density/2, density) (min 1) on room tiles not holding stairs, items or the player; player last on a free room tile. Selection shuffles the candidate list and takes consecutive entries from a random start, wrapping around. On rescue floors the stairs room becomes a monster house.

components.label: Retry-and-fallback floor generator with stairs reachability validation
components.summary: GenerateFloor wraps the layout generators in nested retries: up to 10 layout attempts (rejected unless >=2 rooms and >=30 room tiles; secondary-structure budget zeroed after the first try), then junction marking, water/lava rivers and lakes, spawns, and a BFS-style check that every walkable tile can reach the stairs; up to 10 spawn attempts. Any exhausted loop falls back to a one-room monster house floor, which always succeeds. The dungeon RNG is a 32-bit LCG (x*1566083941+1, upper 16 bits) seeded from a 23-bit per-dungeon preseed, so a floor is reproducible from (dungeon, floor, seed); rescue missions pass that seed to the rescuer.

components.label: Authored fixed rooms embedded in or replacing procedural floors
components.summary: A floor whose fixedRoomNumber is non-zero loads a pre-authored room from the fixedmap archive. Floor-wide fixed rooms (legendary/boss arenas such as Skarmory on Mt. Steel, Groudon in Magma Cavern Pit, Rayquaza on Sky Tower Summit, and the maze bosses) replace generation entirely and skip the stairs check; smaller fixed rooms are placed inside a grid sized so each cell fits the room plus 4 tiles. A zero-size entry falls back to a one-room monster house.

components.label: 24-tick fractional turn scheduler with speed stages
components.summary: Dungeon time advances in fractional ticks 0..23. Each Pokemon's speed stage (species base, usually 1, plus active speed-up counters minus speed-down counters, -1 for paralysis, +1 for Ice types in snow, +1 for an angry Kecleon, clamped 0..4) indexes gSpeedTurns, which says on which ticks it may act: stage 0 acts 3 times per 24 ticks, stage 1 (normal) 6, stage 2 12, stage 3 18, stage 4 every tick. Per tick the order is: wild respawn and Plus/Minus refresh (on normal-speed ticks), leader (player input), team members (up to 3 AI iterations each, then blocked followers re-run nearest-first), then wild Pokemon, then once-per-normal-turn effects. A "turn" in all other timers is one normal-speed action (4 ticks).

components.label: 8-direction tile stepping with no corner cutting and terrain-crossing classes
components.summary: Pokemon occupy one 24x24 px tile and move one tile per action in 8 directions. Each tile caches walkable-neighbour bitmasks for four crossing classes (regular, liquid, crevice/chasm, wall); a diagonal step is only legal if both orthogonal neighbours are non-wall, so walls cannot be corner-cut. Species set the base class (e.g. water types cross water, ghosts walls); the Mobile status or Mobile Scarf grants walls, All-Terrain Hiker grants liquids and chasms, Super Mobile grants walls orthogonally only. Occupied tiles block movement (allies swap with the leader).

components.label: Leader belly that drains per turn and starves HP when empty
components.summary: Only the team leader's belly drains: 0.1 per turn times a multiplier picked from a 20-entry table by an index starting at 10 (x1), shifted by held items/IQ (Tight Belt -> index 0 = no drain; Stamina Band and Energy Saver -1 each = x0.75/x0.5; Diet Ribbon, Heal Ribbon, Munch Belt +1 each = x2/x4/x8), plus 1-4 extra per turn after using linked moves. Messages fire when crossing 20 and 10. At 0 belly the leader takes 1 HP per turn, natural HP regen stops, escalating warnings play, and fainting this way is "fainted from hunger". Food raises belly up to max belly (default 100); eating at full raises max belly, up to 200.

components.label: Accumulator-based HP regeneration for team members
components.summary: Each turn a team member that is not starving or poisoned adds its max HP to an accumulator and gains 1 HP for every regenSpeed units in it, where regenSpeed is a per-species value adjusted by Heal Ribbon (-100), Wish (-220) and Rain Dish in rain (-150), clamped 30..500. Higher max HP therefore heals proportionally faster; wild Pokemon do not regenerate. The same tick decrements every status timer and recomputes speed when a speed counter expires.

components.label: Mystery Dungeon damage formula (atk-def quadratic, level term, no crits for wild)
components.summary: Damage uses physical/special split by move type. A = (Atk + movePower) x stage multiplier (21 stages, 0.25x..2x) + held-item boosts; D = Def x stage multiplier. base = (A - D)/8 + 2/3 x level for team members (wild: unboosted Atk/3). raw = clamp(0.05 x base^2 + 2 x base - D + 10, 1, 999), then x type effectiveness (two-type product via a 4x4 combine table), x0.5 under Reflect/Light Screen, x1.5 on a crit, x move/weather modifiers, x a random 0.875..1.125. Only team members crit (base move odds, +40 Scope Lens/Patsy Band, 40 with Type-Advantage Master on super-effective). Thrown items and seeds use fixed damage.

components.label: Turn-counted status conditions and residual damage
components.summary: Statuses live in exclusive classes (sleep, burn/poison, frozen/wrap/ingrain, cringe/paralysis, reflect, curse, leech seed, sure-shot, invisible, blinker, muzzled), each with a turn counter decremented every turn. Many durations are drawn from configured ranges (sleep 3-7, confusion 6-12, paralysis 1-2, freeze 3-5); burn and poison last until cured. Residual damage uses countdown periods: burn 5 HP every 20 turns, poison 4 every 10, bad poison 6 every 2, wrap 6 and constriction 5 every 2, curse 1/4 max HP every 10. Status gates action: sleep/frozen/petrified skip the turn; confusion randomises facing; blinker restricts attacks to the facing tile.

components.label: Floor weather with periodic chip damage and weather-scaled effects
components.summary: Floors declare one of 8 weathers (clear, sunny, sandstorm, cloudy, rain, hail, fog, snow) or random; moves and abilities can override it for 20 turns. A 10-turn damage counter deals 5 HP to non-Ice Pokemon in hail and to non-Ground/Rock/Steel Pokemon in sandstorm. Weather changes Castform's form and Weather Ball's type, scales Synthesis/Moonlight/Morning Sun healing (50 clear, 80 sun, 1 in fog/snow), and snow raises Ice types' speed stage.

components.label: Per-floor turn limit enforced by an escalating "wind" ejection
components.summary: Each floor starts a counter at the dungeon's turn limit (1000 or 2000 for most dungeons, 600-800 for peaks). It decrements once per leader turn; warnings "Something's stirring" (<250 left), "Something's approaching" (<150) and "It's getting closer" (<50) play with screen effects, and at 0 the team is blown out of the dungeon, a failed exit. Generating the next floor resets the counter.

components.label: Run failure rule - leader faint loses money, held items and half the bag
components.summary: A run fails if the leader faints (or a client or required partner is lost), the wind ejects the team, or the player gives up; 50 exit reasons below 550 are failures and 5 at or above are successes. On a plain failure the town restart removes each bag item with 50% chance, all held items of team members and all carried money; other abnormal returns (e.g. a consumed quicksave) wipe the whole bag. If rescue is allowed the run is instead suspended: the dungeon location and 23-bit seed are quicksaved so a friend can rescue the team via mail or password, after which the run continues. A thief who faints has every item turned into a Plain Seed.

components.label: Periodic wild respawns and ambush monster houses
components.summary: Every 36 turns a new wild Pokemon spawns (species and level from the floor table) unless the floor already holds the cap (10 on floors without a monster house, 4 otherwise; the config names are swapped); after stealing from a Kecleon shop a Kecleon spawns every 5 turns with no cap. Wild Pokemon placed at generation sleep until a team member is adjacent (Racket Band wakes the whole room, Sneak Scarf prevents waking). Entering a monster house the first time drops 8-11 extra Pokemon from above onto free tiles within 4 tiles of the intruder.

components.label: Per-turn monster decision pipeline (item, then move, then movement)
components.summary: RunMonsterAI is the shared brain for allies and wild Pokemon. Each turn: blocking statuses (sleep, freeze, petrify, paralysis-class) pass the turn; blinker, cross-eyed and confusion randomise movement; otherwise the monster considers using an item (AIDecideUseItem), then picks a move or regular attack (ChooseAIMove), then moves (AIMovement). The Dedicated Traveler IQ skill flips this to movement first. Per-monster AI state is an objective (chase target, chase remembered target, roam, leave room, run away, stand still, take item), a target entity and position, and the target's last 4 positions.

components.label: Nearest-visible-target chase with remembered positions and room-exit wandering
components.summary: Wild Pokemon (always tactic "Go after foes") target the nearest visible team member by Chebyshev distance: visible means inside the same room (plus 1-tile border) or within 2 tiles in corridors. Lost targets are chased to their last remembered positions. With no target, a monster in a room walks toward a random room exit (up to 10 picks); in a corridor it keeps going straight and picks a random non-reversing branch at T/+ junctions. Steps head directly toward the target with +-45 degree detours (+-90 while fleeing); blocked monsters wait. Wild Pokemon start asleep and never take stairs.

components.label: Partner AI with player-selectable tactics and follow-the-leader
components.summary: Non-leader team members run the same pipeline but their target selection depends on a tactic chosen from the team menu: Let's go together (follow the leader, fight only what is in reach), Go after foes (hunt nearest foe, else follow), Go the other way (hunt, never follow), Avoid the first hit (hold at 2 tiles), Avoid trouble (flee at <=50% HP), Be patient (stop at <=50% HP), Keep your distance (never attack), Wait there, Get away (always flee). Tactics unlock by level. Followers blocked by allies are re-run nearest-to-leader first so the column moves together; allies with 0 belly stop acting.

components.label: Weighted random move choice with IQ-skill filters and targeting conditions
components.summary: ChooseAIMove sums per-move AI weights (from move data) plus a regular-attack weight that falls as more moves are usable (100 with none, 20/30/40/50 with 1-4), rolls one, and re-verifies a target exists for its range class (adjacent, frontal, room, 2 ahead, line of 10, whole floor, self). Moves can carry an AI condition (random %, target HP <=25%, has status, asleep, ghost). IQ skills reshape the choice: PP Checker drops empty/linked-empty moves, Status Checker skips pointless status moves, Weak-Type Picker turns the roll into an argmax on type effectiveness, Exp. Go-Getter/Efficiency Expert reweight targets, Exclusive Move-User removes the regular attack.

components.label: Probability-table item use and throwing by AI
components.summary: With the Item Master IQ skill (wild Pokemon get it from level 16) monsters roll per-item use probabilities: berries only at <=25% HP (100% if adjacent to an enemy, else 50%), apples when belly <10, status seeds at 80% when adjacent to a foe, thrown spikes/rocks at 70% when an enemy is aligned within 10 tiles. Non-leader allies only use their held item; wild Pokemon also pick up items they stand on and may use orbs.

components.label: Flee to the farthest room exit
components.summary: A monster runs away when terrified (e.g. Stench, 3 turns), at low HP under the Run Away ability or Avoid trouble tactic, or always under Get away. In a room it heads for the exit farthest from the nearest visible enemy whose first step does not close distance; on an exit tile it steps into the corridor; otherwise it moves to the point mirrored away from the enemy. Fleeing monsters cannot attack, use or pick up items.

components.label: IQ points unlocking passive skills (gummi-fed)
components.summary: Each team Pokemon has IQ (1..999) raised mainly by eating Gummis (+7 for a matching type, +1..4 otherwise). 23 IQ skills unlock at point thresholds (e.g. Item Catcher 1, Status Checker 25, Trap Avoider 140, Energy Saver 250, All-Terrain Hiker 400, Super Mobile 990) and can be toggled. Most change AI behaviour of allies (target choice, hazard avoidance, item use); some change rules (Energy Saver halves belly drain index, Quick Dodger, Type-Advantage Master crits). Wild Pokemon get a fixed set.

components.label: 20-slot shared team bag, held items, stacking throwables and sticky items
components.summary: The team shares one 20-slot bag; each Pokemon also has one held-item slot whose passive effect applies while held (bands, scarves, ribbons). Only thrown items (sticks, spikes, rocks) stack, up to 99. Poke picked up converts straight to money. Items can be sticky (unusable, cleared on returning to town). Categories: thrown (line projectiles or arcing rocks), food (belly), berries/seeds (heal, status, level, damage), vitamins (+3 stat), gummis (IQ), orbs (cast a move once), TMs (become a reusable Used TM), held gear. Some dungeons cap or forbid carried items on entry.

components.label: Straight-line and arcing thrown items
components.summary: Line throwables fly along one of 8 directions up to 10 tiles and hit the first Pokemon (90% hit chance; Whiff Specs/Lock-on Specs/Dodge Scarf override); arcing rocks (Gravelerock, Geo Pebble) fly over obstacles to a target within 10 tiles for fixed damage. Long Toss/Pierce raise range to 99 and pass through targets. Pokemon with free hands may catch thrown items. L+R throws the set item.

components.label: Hidden floor traps with 20 effects
components.summary: Traps spawn hidden (Wonder Tiles visible) on room tiles from a per-floor weighted table. A team member stepping on a hidden trap triggers it 85% of the time and reveals it; visible traps always trigger. Effects span damage (Chestnut 10, Spiked Tile 20, explosions), status (sleep, confusion, poison, slow), inventory attacks (Sticky, Grimy 30% per food, Trip knocks off held item), PP/move sabotage (PP-Zero, Seal), displacement (Warp, Gust, Pitfall drops to the next floor with 5 damage), and spawning (Summon 2-4 Pokemon, Pokemon Trap turns room items into Pokemon). Trap Scarf prevents triggers; Trap Seer reveals on step; Trap Avoider makes AI avoid visible traps.

components.label: In-dungeon Kecleon shop with pay-on-exit and thief state
components.summary: Shop rooms hold priced merchandise (flag IN_SHOP). Picking items up adds to a running bill; leaving the shop tiles prompts payment, and items dropped on shop tiles can be sold. Walking off with unpaid goods sets the thief state for the floor: all Kecleon turn hostile (+1 speed), a Kecleon spawns every 5 turns with no cap, Pokemon Traps spawn Kecleon, Escape Orbs fail, the leader cannot be changed, and fainting turns every item into a Plain Seed. Successfully leaving as a thief increments a thieving counter.

components.label: Poke currency, town shops and service prices
components.summary: Money (Poke) is capped at 99,999 carried. Sources are floor piles (value from a 100-entry table, capped per floor at moneyUpperBound x 40), mission rewards and selling. Sinks are the Kecleon brothers' town shop (8 item slots and 4 wares slots, restocked from story-stage item sets), Gulpin's move-linking (150 Poke), Wigglytuff's friend areas (100 to 9,500 Poke) and in-dungeon Kecleon shops. Defeat zeroes carried money.

components.label: Kangaskhan storage and Persian bank as defeat-proof stores
components.summary: Kangaskhan storage keeps up to 999 of each of the 240 item ids (not Poke or Used TMs) and Felicity Bank holds up to 9,999,999 Poke with no interest. Neither is exposed to dungeon defeat, so they are the safe side of a carry-versus-store trade-off: items and money must be withdrawn into the 20-slot bag / 99,999 wallet before an expedition to be usable.

components.label: Multi-floor mystery dungeons with stairs and per-dungeon rule sets
components.summary: An expedition is a linear sequence of freshly generated floors (3 to 99); stepping on the stairs and confirming generates the next floor and resets the turn limit, and clearing the last floor ends the run as a success. 98 dungeon entries carry rule flags: stairs up or down, recruiting enabled, rescues allowed, max items carried, max party size, keep money, level reset to 1 (Wish Cave, Joyous Tower, Purity Forest), checkpoint, auto-save before entry, required HMs and turn limit. A taken job on a floor adds its client or target to that floor.

components.label: Player-controlled leader with up to three AI partners (body-size budget)
components.summary: The player controls the leader; up to 3 other team members follow under AI. Team size is limited to 4 members and a body-size budget of 6 (large species take more slots), and per dungeon to maxPartyMembers. Only the leader drains belly; the leader fainting ends the run, while a partner fainting just removes it (unless it is a client or required partner, which forces a loss). Leader switching unlocks late in the story and is barred in some dungeons and while a thief.

components.label: Defeat-to-recruit roll gated by friend-area ownership
components.summary: When a team member defeats a wild Pokemon from an adjacent tile in a dungeon that allows recruiting, the game rolls rand(1000) < species recruit rate + 100 (Friend Bow) + a level bonus (0 below level 30, rising to 240 at 90+). The species' friend area must already be owned and the team must have a free member slot and body-size room; legendaries can join once. A recruit joins immediately at its current level with IQ 1, and is stored in its friend area when not on the team.

components.label: Purchasable friend areas as recruitment licences and roster storage
components.summary: The 57 friend areas each house a fixed set of species and act as both licence and box: a species can only be recruited once its area is owned, and recruits rest there. Areas are bought from Wigglytuff (19 during the story, 26 post-game, 100 to 9,500 Poke), granted by Wonder Mail rewards (4) or by legendary requests (8). Area capacity limits how many can be kept; when full, one must be released.

components.label: Shared full exp per KO, levels to 100, story-gated evolution
components.summary: Defeating a wild Pokemon gives every team member on the floor the full exp (not split): yield + yield x (level-1)/10, x1.5 or x0.5 by modifiers, minimum 1, total capped at 9,999,999. Levels run to 100 using per-species level tables that add HP and Atk/SpAtk/Def/SpDef. Some dungeons reset levels to 1 for the visit. Evolution happens only at Luminous Cave after the story unlocks it, requiring level/IQ/item conditions and an owned, non-full friend area for the evolved form.

components.label: Procedurally generated rescue jobs from a board and mailbox
components.summary: Pelipper's board regenerates 5-8 jobs each day (plus story jobs) and the mailbox up to 4. A job picks an unlocked dungeon, a floor in its back half, a type (rescue client 2/8, rescue target 2/8, escort 2/8, find item 1/8, deliver item 1/8), client/target species, item and reward. Difficulty comes from a per-floor table (+2 for escort) and maps to rank E..S/star; rewards are money ((rank+1) x 100 on the board, x200 by mail), items, or a friend area. Up to 8 jobs can be taken; on the job floor the target appears and talking to it completes the job and offers to leave the dungeon.

components.label: Rescue team rank from cumulative job points
components.summary: Job rewards add rank points; rank is the first threshold above the total: Normal (<50), Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Lucario (>=15000). Rank mostly signals status: at Normal rank escort jobs are not offered, and Lucario rank unlocks a news item; no storage or shop perks were found.

components.label: Wonder Mail 24-character job passwords
components.summary: A job can be shared as a 24-character password over a 32-symbol alphabet (5 bits each = 120 bits): byte 0 is an additive checksum over the other 14 bytes, the payload packs mail type, mission type, client, target, item, reward, friend area, a 24-bit dungeon seed, dungeon and floor (93 bits), and character positions are shuffled by a fixed 24-entry permutation (no encryption). Decoded mail is validated (legal dungeon and floor, allowed species, no thrown items, friend-area rewards only above rank E) and becomes a mailbox job with a reproducible floor.

components.label: Asynchronous friend rescue via SOS / A-OK / Thank-You passwords or link
components.summary: When a team faints in a dungeon that allows rescues, the run is suspended and an SOS mail (dungeon, floor, seed, leader species, ids, player name, rescues left) is created and exported as a 54-character password or over link. Another player imports it, enters the same seeded dungeon as "out on rescue" with their own team, and on reaching the floor sends back an A-OK mail; importing it revives the original team where it fell. A Thank-You mail can carry a reward item back. Each failed rescue decrements rescuesAllowed (10 or 30 per dungeon).

components.label: Scenario-stage flags gating jobs, recruiting, evolution and dungeons
components.summary: Progress is a main-scenario (stage, sub-stage) pair plus sub-scenarios in script variables; CheckQuest derives gates from it: job board after (4,3), recruiting after (5,0), post-game after stage 17, evolution after (18,2), leader change after (18,3). Legendary encounters and new dungeons open on further stages or sub-scenarios; dungeon clears are recorded per dungeon and the return map and script are chosen from the run result.

components.label: Boss floors and legendary encounters at dungeon ends
components.summary: Story dungeons end on fixed-room boss floors (Skarmory, Team Meanies, Zapdos, Moltres, Articuno, Groudon, Rayquaza, Mewtwo, Jirachi, etc.) entered through dedicated cutscene routines; defeating them advances the story, and post-game legendaries become recruitable once each.

components.label: Increment two bytes only while each is below its threshold
components.summary: The helper increments object+0x84 when its unsigned byte value is below 16 and independently increments+0x85 when below 10. Values already at or above a threshold are left unchanged, so this is directional threshold-limited growth rather than a clamp that repairs arbitrary out-of-range states; actor and resource meanings are unknown.

components.label: Conditionally remap a mask and query one or two context bitfields
components.summary: Three verified leaf helpers use a mode halfword at object+0x7e and a global context pointer at 0x03001270. If mode=0 or(mask&0xf0)=0, the mask is unchanged; otherwise the full32-bit mask shifts right1 when(mask&0xa0)!=0 and left1 otherwise, then intersects context+4. Entry 0x08016434 returns whether that intersection is zero, while 0x08016480 additionally intersects context+6; no gameplay interpretation of the mode or context bits is established.

components.label: Query a bit using an8-bit byte index
components.summary: The helper computes byteIndex=(input>>3)&255, loads one byte from global context+0xc2+byteIndex and returns the selected bit. Its explicit shift-count arithmetic reduces to input&7, so higher input bits beyond bit10 do not affect the result; the logical query aliases modulo2048, but the actual allocated bitset size remains unverified.

evidence.ref: ((i - 8*((i>>3)&255)) &255) == (i&7); byte index retains bits3..10, giving index alias period2048.

components.label: Initialize three bytes to255 and a fourth to0
components.summary: The helper follows the pointer stored at 0x03000fc0 and writes255 to offsets 0x72,0x73 and 0x74, then0 to+0x75. These may be sentinels and a count/flag, but that interpretation is not proven; only the four byte values and offsets are established.

components.label: Reset BG2 and BG3 affine state to identity
components.summary: Instructions use halfword writes to zero both affine reference origins and off-diagonal coefficients while setting PA and PD to 256 for BG2 and BG3. This gives the native8.8 identity coefficient1.0, but a setup routine alone does not show that an affine layer is enabled or visibly used in the captured phases.

components.label: Configure DMA0 with a structure-owned source and BG1 scroll destination
components.summary: The helper first disables DMA0 control, loads the source pointer from structure+0x18, targets 0x04000014 and writes combined control/count 0xa2600001. The retained capture separately records HBlank DMA0 to that BG-scroll destination; this corroborates hardware use but does not identify the owning scene, camera model or table-generation rule.

components.label: Copy selected object fields into a36-byte indexed record
components.summary: A destination pointer from object+0x0c and raw index select a36-byte record. Instructions gather eight32-bit words from source offsets 0x10,0x14,0x48,0x4c,0x58,0x5c,0x60,0x64 and two16-bit values from 0x68,0x6a into consecutive destination fields; no history-buffer, rewind or persistence role is established by this helper.

components.label: Four background scroll buffers with modulo-512 offsets
components.summary: The native setter at 0x08000e20 stores horizontal and vertical offsets for a selected background in one of four 0x810-byte contexts, masks each offset to nine bits and marks its scroll state dirty. A recovered renderer prefix sends those buffers to BG0–BG3 scroll registers, optionally adding signed layer-specific shake offsets. This is a reusable display/camera seam, not a recovered complete player camera or world coordinate model.

games.name: Sonic Advance

components.label: Language select, SEGA logo, title and task-driven mode flow
components.summary: The USA cart boots to a two-option language select (Japanese/English), then a 'Presented by SEGA' logo, an intro animation and the title screen ('PRESS START'), followed by a main menu with single player, multiplayer, time attack, options and a Tiny Chao Garden entry. Flow is not a central mode switch but chained task callbacks (gCurTask->main reassignment) with brightness fades between screens.

evidence.ref: USA self-decompilation: 0x08001224 input edges and0x080016AC task callback dispatch; research/requests/sonic-self-decomp-evidence.json
capture:attract:frame 300 keyframe (language select, Japanese/English only, idles without input)

components.label: Title idle timer and rotating recorded-input attract demos
components.summary: After 900 idle frames on the title the game starts one of four attract demos in rotation, each a fixed (character, level) pair driven by recorded input through the normal stage code with a 'DEMO PLAY' sprite. The demo manager forces default button mapping and normal difficulty and ends playback after 30 s of stage time or on a real button press.

evidence.ref: capture:attract:frames 0-3600 (no input; stuck on language select, so no demo observed)

components.label: Four-character select, per-character course unlocks and CPU-Tails secret code
components.summary: Single player picks Sonic, Tails, Knuckles or Amy; each character keeps its own highest unlocked level (unlockedLevels[character]) and a fresh character starts directly at Neo Green Hill act 1 while others go through course select. A nine-key input on character select (Up, Right, Down, Right, L, Right, R, Right, A) turns on a CPU partner Tails that follows the player.

components.label: Single flash save with emeralds, per-character progress, settings and records
components.summary: One SaveGame record is kept in flash (two-sector rotation with erase/program/verify) holding a magic number, per-character unlocked level, player name, difficulty, language, time-limit toggle, button layout, a chaos-emerald bitfield, time-attack records, multiplayer scores, total score and a checksum. Saving happens on results screens, not at in-level save points.

components.label: Lives, time-over and game over
components.summary: Single player starts with 3 lives (1 in some modes). Death (ringless hit, pit, drowning, or time over at 10:00 when the time limit is enabled) costs a life and restarts from the last checkpoint; reaching zero shows game over. Extra lives come from 1-UP boxes, every 100 rings and every 50,000 points.

components.label: Time attack, link multiplayer modes and Tiny Chao Garden
components.summary: Besides the story, the game offers time attack (best three times per course and character), link-cable multiplayer (race, Chao hunt, team play, and a single-pak ring-collection mode sent by multiboot) and a Tiny Chao Garden mini-game. Time attack and multiplayer force normal difficulty for the session.

components.label: Mode-0 stage stack of two metatile collision layers plus scenery BG
components.summary: Stages run in DISPCNT mode 0 with BG1 (front metatile layer, priority 1), BG2 (back metatile layer, priority 2) and BG3 (zone scenery, priority 3), OBJ in 1D mapping and WIN0 enabled. The two metatile layers mirror the two collision layers the player can switch between (loops). The extra stage switches to mode 1 with BG0-BG2.

components.label: Per-scanline BG scroll table for cloud bands and perspective water
components.summary: Zone background updaters fill a 160-entry horizontal-offset table that an HBlank copy writes into a BG scroll register each line. In Neo Green Hill the top bands scroll on a timer at three speeds (clouds), middle rows stay static, and the bottom 'water' rows scroll by (line-86)/256 of camera X so lower lines move faster, giving a perspective water plane. Other zones (2 interior, 3, 6, 7 act 2) use the same mechanism.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:hblank_dma_targets ch0->0x04000018 and ch0->0x0400001C (BG2/BG3 HOFS), bg_scroll hdma_frames_ge32=4268

components.label: Title emblem zoom with mode-1 affine BG2
components.summary: The title screen switches to mode 1 and scales the affine BG2 emblem from a large magnification down to 1:1 over about 12 frames (BG2PA/PD ramp 0x41 -> 0x100) before showing PRESS START. Only one affine OBJ is ever visible in the captured front end.

components.label: Sprite-scaled pseudo-3D special stage over palette-cycled backgrounds
components.summary: The special stage stays in tile mode 0 (DISPCNT 0x1C40) with four text BG panels and a full background; depth is faked by OBJ affine scaling of rings, bombs and the character as a forward-progress counter advances, while palette-loader tasks cycle 'big orthogonal' and 'small diagonal' light palettes per stage.

evidence.ref: sa2:src/game/sa1/special_stage/main.c (tf->qScaleX/qScaleY, Div(0x10000, qScale) into OAM affine)

components.label: Brightness fades and zig-zag title-card wipe
components.summary: Screen transitions use BLDY brightness fades (BLDCNT 0x3FFF/0x3F9F style full-screen fades), a zig-zag colour wipe at act start, and windows to mask regions; capture shows brightness fade and windows used but no alpha blending or mosaic in the observed front end and first act.

evidence.ref: capture:derived flags brightness_fade=true, windows=true, alpha_blend=false, mosaic=false
capture:frontend:frame 1600 keyframe (zig-zag wipe at act start)

components.label: Dead-zone follow camera with air band, look up/down and spindash hold
components.summary: The camera target is the player centred (x-120, y-80 plus a sprite-height offset that eases 5 px/frame). Horizontally the camera only moves once the target leaves an 8 px dead band and then by at most 16 px/frame; there is no velocity look-ahead in SA1 (SA2 added one). Vertically the dead band is 0 on ground and grows by 4 px/frame to 24 px in the air, with a 12 px/frame cap. Holding Up/Down while standing still for 120 frames pans the view 2 px/frame to 72 px up or 60 px down. Releasing a spindash freezes the camera for 10 frames, letting the player outrun the screen.

components.label: Side-view orthographic stages with rotating-surface character
components.summary: Regular acts are orthographic side views; the player sprite is rotated to the surface angle while running on slopes, walls and ceilings. Special stages switch to a scaled-sprite pseudo-3D view.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:frame 2200 keyframe (side-view Neo Green Hill with pause overlay)

components.label: Scalar ground-speed momentum with turnaround skid and friction
components.summary: Holding a direction adds 8/256 px/frame^2 to ground speed up to a 4.5 px/frame cap, but the cap only stops acceleration: speed already above it (from slopes, springs, spindash) is kept. Pressing against the motion subtracts 96/256 px/frame^2 (a skid with a brake sound above 3 px/frame) and, when it crosses zero, snaps to 96/256 px/frame in the new direction. With no direction held a flat 8/256 px/frame^2 friction applies. Ground speed is projected onto the surface angle every frame to produce the air-velocity used for movement.

evidence.ref: USA self-decompilation: 0x08047078 tangent projection; actor0x03005A20 derived at0x080454D8; research/requests/sonic-self-decomp-evidence.json

components.label: Slope gravity on ground speed, roll asymmetry and steep-surface slip
components.summary: Each grounded frame adds a slope term proportional to sin(surface angle): 3/32 of the sine (max 24/256 px/frame^2) when running, and 60/256 of the sine when rolling, quartered when it opposes motion (uphill). The run term is applied only while moving and away from ceilings. On a surface steeper than 45 degrees, ground speed below 1.875 px/frame drops the player off (air state) and locks horizontal control for 30 frames; that is what forces momentum into loops and quarter-pipes.

evidence.ref: USA self-decompilation: 0x08046F78 slope acceleration and0x08047078 tangent projection; research/requests/sonic-self-decomp-evidence.json

components.label: Height-map terrain sensors with 256-step surface angles
components.summary: Collision data per level is a metatile map of 8x8 tiles carrying a height map, a per-tile angle and flags, on two layers. Ground, wall and ceiling probes return signed distances; grounded movement snaps to the floor and takes its angle, a forward probe stops the player at walls (zeroing ground speed and leaving the roll), and a jump needs at least 4 px of headroom along the surface normal. In the air the sprite angle relaxes back to upright by 2/256 turn per frame.

evidence.ref: research/requests/sonic-recovered-contact.package.json; Own USA scanner/profile/geometry/headroom/attachedresponse closure; 9216vectors each scanner,headroom,attachedresponse over18geometrydefinitions. Airborne landingresponse outsidebundle.

USA self-decompilation: 0x08040080 metatile lookup and0x0803FE10/0x0803FF50 both-axis profile/angle probes,23040 original-Thumb comparisons over18 stage definitions; 0x0804386C terrain/contact quadrant dispatch and0x08047078 angle projection; research/requests/sonic-self-decomp-evidence.json

components.label: Loops via two collision layers and layer-toggle triggers
components.summary: Every map has a front and back collision layer; the player carries a layer bit. Invisible rectangular toggle objects set or clear that bit when the player's position is inside them, so a loop's entry and exit can be on different layers while the player runs 360 degrees around using the angle-following ground physics. The CPU partner copies the leader's layer.

components.label: Surface-normal jump, release cap and light gravity without terminal velocity
components.summary: Jump adds 4.875 px/frame along the surface normal (so jumping off a wall or slope keeps tangential momentum) and puts Sonic, Tails and Knuckles into a rolled, damaging state. Gravity is 42/256 px/frame^2. Releasing the button while rising faster than 3 px/frame caps upward speed at 3. SA1 has no fall-speed cap (SA2 added one); non-jump launches are capped at 11.8125 px/frame upward. While rising, horizontal speed bleeds 1/32 per frame (air drag).

evidence.ref: research/requests/sonic-recovered-jump.package.json; Own USA completejump initializer0x0804421C, all4characters, nativeheadroom/hitbox/sound;1000original-vs-emittedvectors. Recovered release dispatch0x0804463C separatelyqualified; native gravity42/12 remains Sonicbaseline.
USA self-decompilation: 0x0804421C jump,0x0804463C release,0x080470B4 integration,0x08047100 gravity; research/requests/sonic-self-decomp-evidence.json

components.label: Double-rate air acceleration capped at run speed
components.summary: Airborne, left/right add twice the ground acceleration (16/256 px/frame^2) up to the current max speed, again without reducing speed already above it, and turn the character unless bouncing. Control is ignored while in the hurt state.

evidence.ref: research/requests/sonic-recovered-air-control.package.json; Own USA aircontrol0x0804456C and release/airability0x0804463C:24192basevectors+24nativecharacterabilitycases. Inheritedoverspeed preserved; hurt15 skipssteering. Abilitybody/taskstateclosure partial.

components.label: Down-to-roll with low friction and attack hitbox
components.summary: Pressing Down while moving curls Sonic, Tails or Knuckles into a roll (damaging, shorter hitbox). A rolling player cannot accelerate; friction is half the acceleration (4/256 px/frame^2), pressing against the roll decelerates 24/256 px/frame^2 and turns around at 96/256, and rolling slopes use the stronger downhill factor. When the roll stops, it uncurls to crouch or stand; in forced-roll tubes (MOVESTATE_200) it is re-launched at 3 px/frame.

components.label: Crouch-charged spin dash with decaying charge and release table
components.summary: From a crouch, Jump starts a spin dash; each further Jump press adds 2 charge units and a pitched rev sound, charge decays by 1/32 per frame, and releasing Down launches at a table speed indexed by the integer charge (6.0 to 9.0 px/frame in 0.375 steps; 8.25 to 11.25 in the boosted mode). Because the code clamps with MAX(charge+2, 8), the first press already gives a full charge (index 8); rapid re-presses can reach index 9, which reads the next table. The camera freezes for 10 frames on release.

components.label: Springs, dash panels and special springs as speed injectors
components.summary: Springs set vertical or horizontal speed to one of four strengths (7.5, 9, 10.5, 12 px/frame) or a per-object custom value, cancel flight, and multiply by 1.5 if Amy triggers them with her hammer. Diagonal springs set both axes. Dash panels (boosters) set ground speed to 12 px/frame if it is below 9. Special springs launch upward at 7.5 px/frame and, the first time, carry the player off-screen into the special stage.

components.label: Underwater constant set, surface splash and drowning countdown
components.summary: Below the water level the player's speed caps and accelerations halve, gravity drops to 12/256 and jumps to 2.625 px/frame. Entering halves X and quarters Y speed; leaving doubles Y speed. An air timer of 30 s counts down with countdown digits from 12 s, music switch near 11 s, and death at zero; air bubbles reset it.

components.label: Rail grinding on a second layer
components.summary: Grind rails put the player in a rail state where ground speed loses 8/256 px/frame^2 (twice that if holding Left), never drops below 0.75 px/frame, and gains a 5/32 sine slope term when Down or Right is held. Jumping off flips the collision layer and launches at the normal jump speed.

components.label: Sonic: insta-shield, double-tap air dash and B-button ground combo
components.summary: Sonic's second Jump press in the air fires an insta-shield burst; double-tapping a direction in the air (second tap 4-10 frames after the first) gives a horizontal air dash of max_speed/4 and zeroes vertical speed. On the ground, B starts a 2 px/frame skid attack, a second B a 3 px/frame somersault, then a slide (32/256 friction) or a spinning back-jump on Jump.

components.label: Tails: flap-to-rise flight with an 8 s stamina timer
components.summary: Pressing Jump again in the air starts flight. Each flap applies 24/256 px/frame^2 upward for up to 31 frames while upward speed is under 0.75 px/frame, then Tails sinks with 8/256 px/frame^2 (16/256 when MOVESTATE_10000) until Jump re-flaps. The stamina counter starts at 240 and ticks every other frame (8 s); at zero Tails is exhausted and falls. Flight cannot rise above the camera top bound. Underwater it becomes swimming.

components.label: Knuckles: accelerating glide, steerable turn, wall climb and wall jump
components.summary: Second Jump in the air starts a glide at 3 px/frame horizontally (1.5 underwater) with vertical speed nudged 24/256 per frame toward a 0.5 px/frame descent. Glide speed grows 6/256 per frame below 3 and 3/256 per frame up to 18 px/frame when not turning; pressing the opposite direction swings a heading angle 2 steps per frame so the X velocity follows cos(heading). Touching a wall grabs it: Up/Down climbs at 0.75 px/frame (0.5 underwater) and Jump kicks off at 3 px/frame away and 2.625 up. Ground B is a punch adding 3 px/frame.

components.label: Amy: hammer attacks, hammer jump and no rolling
components.summary: Amy never rolls or spin-dashes and her normal jump is not an attack. B on the ground swings the hammer (ground speed bleeds 0.375 px/frame per frame), Down+B (B with Down while grounded) performs a high hammer jump at 6.0 px/frame (3.375 underwater), Down+Jump is a forward hammer dash (4.0 forward, 1.25 up). In the air B swings or, with Down, does a downward hammer swirl that stops X speed. Hammer hits on springs multiply the launch by 1.5.

components.label: Four playable characters sharing one physics core with per-character actions
components.summary: All four characters use the same ground, slope, jump and water constants and differ only in their action layer (mid-air action, ground B action, roll/spin dash availability). Each frame the player task dispatches to a per-character state function over the (in_air, spin_attack) state pair.

components.label: Rings as one-hit buffer with full scatter on damage
components.summary: Getting hit with no shield and at least one ring drops all rings (up to 48 are spawned as collectible scatter, the rest are lost), knocks the player back 1.5 px/frame away and 3 px/frame up (halved underwater) and grants 120 frames of invulnerability. A hit with zero rings is death; a shield absorbs one hit and is consumed instead. Only player 1 loses rings; the CPU partner just gets knocked back. Invincibility makes the body hitbox destroy enemies.

components.label: Dropped-ring fan, bounce and expiry
components.summary: Lost rings spawn in symmetric pairs around a fan whose speed starts at about 4.5 px/frame and steps through angles in 16-unit increments, halving magnitude per ring of 16; each falls at 18/256 px/frame^2, bounces off floors with -0.75 restitution, cannot be re-collected for the first 32 frames, blinks in its last 32 frames and vanishes after 256 frames. The extra stage uses 7/256 gravity.

components.label: Attack-hitbox enemy kills with bounce and landing-reset score chain
components.summary: The player sprite has a body hitbox and an attack hitbox that is active while rolled, spin-dashing or using a character attack. An enemy overlapping the attack hitbox is destroyed (dust cloud, freed animal) and, if the player was falling, vertical speed is reflected upward; overlapping only the body hitbox damages the player unless invincible. Consecutive kills before touching ground score 100, 200, 400, 800, then 1000 each.

components.label: Monitor power-ups
components.summary: Breaking an item box grants its content after a 60-frame display delay. Contents are 1-UP, normal shield (absorbs one hit), magnetic shield (also pulls nearby rings), 20 s invincibility (with its own music), 20 s speed shoes (doubles max speed, acceleration and deceleration and doubles music tempo), random rings, 5 or 10 rings.

components.label: Checkpoint posts storing respawn position and time
components.summary: Touching a checkpoint post stores its position and the current stage time on the player; after a death the act restarts there with the stored time. Special springs also overwrite the checkpoint so the player returns to the spring after a special stage.

components.label: Easy/Normal difficulty that thins enemies and shortens bosses
components.summary: An options setting picks Normal or Easy. Easy removes selected badnik placements in early zones (Buzzer in zone 1, Leon in zone 5 and others) and starts zone bosses two hits down (8 -> 6 hits for Mecha Knuckles and the Super Egg Robo). Time attack, race, multiplayer and demos always run on Normal.

components.label: Pseudo-3D ring-quota special stage with two checkpoints
components.summary: Entered through a hidden special spring, the stage moves the character forward through depth while the player steers within a +-134 x +-94 px plane, collecting rings and avoiding hazards. There are two ring gates: the first needs the stage's first quota (60 to 100) and the second twice that (120 to 200); falling short shows a NOT ENOUGH RINGS message and fades out without an emerald. Forward speed starts at 8 depth units/frame and can be boosted by 1.5x up to 12.

components.label: Super Sonic flight with draining ring timer in the extra stage
components.summary: The Moon extra stage turns Sonic into Super Sonic flying in an auto-scrolling arena (scroll 8 px/frame, wrapping every 2688 px). Rings start at 50 and drain one per second, with a warning sound at 10 or fewer; reaching 0 kills. Hits from the Super Egg Robo only knock Super Sonic back (3 px/frame, 30 invulnerability frames, 24-frame control lock) and capsules released by the boss refill rings.

components.label: CPU Tails replaying the leader's inputs with a 20-frame delay
components.summary: With the partner code entered, a second Player struct runs Tails on the same physics, fed by the leader's held input from 20 frames earlier (a 60-frame input history ring). It overrides horizontal input to close a 16 px gap, turns to face the leader when idle, presses Jump when the leader is 80+ px higher or when falling behind in the air, copies the leader's collision layer, and if left far off-screen respawns by flying in from a camera-relative point. The partner can break enemies and collect rings but never loses rings.

components.label: Patrol-then-charge badnik (Rhinotank)
components.summary: Rhinotank patrols a map-defined span at 0.625 px/frame, turning at its ends. If the player is within 80 px ahead and between 32 px above and 8 px below, it revs and charges at 3 px/frame until the span end. It is destroyed by any attack-hitbox contact.

components.label: Patrolling ranged badniks (Buzzer, Kiki)
components.summary: Buzzer flies a map-defined span at 1 px/frame and, when the player is up to 96 px below and inside a forward window, stops and fires a projectile downward. Kiki throws projectiles whose horizontal speed is scaled to the player's distance so they land near the player.

components.label: Hit-counter Eggman bosses with post-hit invulnerability and pinch phase
components.summary: Each zone ends with an Eggman machine that takes a fixed number of hits (7-8 on Normal, 2 fewer on Easy) and is invulnerable for 32 frames after each hit. Hits come from attack-hitbox contact by the player or partner; body contact hurts. The Egg Hammer Tank (zone 1) speeds up after its 5th hit and switches to a defeat sequence at 7. X Zone chains three more bosses and the Moon hosts the Super Egg Robo.

components.label: Linear zones of two acts with end-of-act-2 bosses, unlocked per character
components.summary: Story mode is linear: Neo Green Hill, Secret Base, Casino Paradise, Ice Mountain and Angel Island each have two acts with a boss at the end of act 2; zone 6 is Egg Rocket (act 1, with a 3-minute launch countdown subtracted from the course time) and Cosmic Angel (act 2); zone 7 is X Zone (boss rush) and The Moon (extra). Clearing an act raises unlockedLevels for the current character, which the course select reads.

components.label: Seven emeralds plus all-character clears gate the extra stage
components.summary: Each special stage awards one bit of a 7-bit chaos-emerald field shared by all characters. The Moon (Super Sonic vs Super Egg Robo) and the true ending happen only if the current character is Sonic, all 7 emeralds are held, and all four characters have cleared beyond level 12 (X Zone). Otherwise the X Zone clear ends the game.

components.label: Ring loop: placed and boxed sources, damage sink, life converter
components.summary: Rings come from fixed level placements, item boxes and re-collected scatter; they are spent only by damage (all lost, up to 48 recoverable). Every crossing of a multiple of 100 rings gives an extra life (single player, not in the extra stage), and at the goal each ring is worth 100 points. In the extra stage rings become a draining countdown.

components.label: Score from enemy chains and end-of-act time and ring bonuses
components.summary: Score comes from enemy chains (100-1000), item boxes and the act-clear tally of a time bonus (80,000 under 30 s down to 0 at 6:00 or later) plus 100 per ring. Every 50,000 points gives an extra life.

components.label: Ring, time and lives counters with warning flashes
components.summary: The stage HUD shows the ring count and an M:SS:cc timer top-left and the character's life icon with the lives count bottom-left. Digits flash red when under a minute remains in timed modes or past 9:00 of the 10-minute limit; drowning shows countdown numbers over the player.

components.label: Start pause and two-layout button mapping
components.summary: Start pauses with a PAUSE banner and resumes on Start (time attack also allows a retry with A). Jump and attack are mapped to A/B with a reversible layout stored in the save; demos force the default layout.

components.label: Wordless intro, act transitions and emerald-dependent endings
components.summary: Story is delivered without dialogue through an animated intro, sprite cutscenes between zones (including a Tornado rescue and an Egg Rocket launch sequence), and staff credits whose ending differs with the emerald count.

components.label: Bright cartoon island-to-space Eggman story
components.summary: Sonic and friends cross bright tropical, casino, ice and ancient-island zones to Eggman's rocket and space station, then the Moon; enemies are robot 'badniks' that free trapped animals when broken. Tone is upbeat, fast and arcade-like.

components.label: MP2K (m4a) sequencer at a 10.5 kHz mix rate with PSG
components.summary: Audio uses Nintendo's m4a/MP2K library (src/lib/m4a linked into the SA1 build) with 174 MIDI-derived songs. Captures show DirectSound A and B active nearly every frame at 10512 Hz and all four PSG channels used. Pitch control is used for the spindash rev and tempo control for speed shoes.

components.label: Per-act tracks with power-up, drowning and boss overrides
components.summary: Each act has its own track; boss fights, invincibility, drowning and special stages switch tracks, speed shoes double the BGM tempo for 20 s, and 1-UPs queue a jingle. Act clear plays a different jingle for normal acts, boss acts, X Zone and the Moon.

sourceReferences: https://github.com/SAT-R/sa2 @ 393357f7c9d46b5c10b6c41a57b80fe3b58f3c8d (no license file; local/decomps/sa2). SA1 is built with GAME_NAME=sa1 (config.mk GAME_REGION EUROPE, sa1.sha1 eb00f101... = 'Sonic Advance (Europe) (En,Ja,Fr,De,Es)' per README), not our USA ASOE ROM. SA1 code lives in src/game/sa1/** (173 .c files, ~82k lines) plus engine code shared with SA2 in src/game/shared/** behind '#if GAME == GAME_SA1' guards; sa1_ldscript links only C objects (no asm/*.o), with ~159 function bodies still pulled from asm/non_matching (*sa1*). Data tables are incbin'd from a EU baserom, so values were cross-checked in the USA ROM where noted.

games.name: Wario Land 4

components.label: Explicit game-mode routing
components.summary: The main loop dispatches cutscenes, file selection, stage selection, gameplay, pause, shop, minigames, demo and credits. Stage selection enters a minigame for stage IDs 6, 12, 18 and 24, while exit types select different return sequences.

components.label: Run-length recorded-input demo
components.summary: Playback replaces held and newly pressed buttons using recorded masks and durations. Real held input or an exhausted/sentinel sequence injects Start to end the playback, so a visible gameplay image alone does not establish human control.

components.label: Two save files and checked SRAM writes
components.summary: The save interface offers two selected files and implements bytewise write verification with at most three attempts. SRAM helper tables assign distinct ranges to the two files; verified bytes do not establish higher-level atomic recovery or checksum guarantees.

components.label: Guarded button-chord soft reset
components.summary: A+B+Start+Select routes to the soft-reset game mode when reset is enabled. The handler ignores the chord during an already active soft reset or when the disable flag is set.

components.label: Conditional Start pause routing
components.summary: Start can request the pause mode only when the player pause timer and an additional actor status byte permit it. Boss-related states may route to BossPause instead; pause can return to gameplay, leave a stage, or soft reset.

components.label: Context and difficulty-dependent starting health
components.summary: Ordinary super-hard stages initialize current health to one. Golden-passage or boss contexts instead initialize eight on normal difficulty and four otherwise; that branch precedes the ordinary super-hard branch.

components.label: Eight-heart health and recovery gauges
components.summary: Separate graphics tables represent zero through eight hearts, a flashing one-heart state, and a second gauge with eight fill increments. The inspected gameplay frame visibly shows the heart row; the exact refill-to-heart conversion timing remains unverified.

components.label: Jewel quadrants and CD status artwork
components.summary: The HUD source defines full and partial variants for four jewel quadrants and a CD icon. These are authored display assets associated with collection state; their complete update policy has not been traced.

components.label: Mutually exclusive reaction control regimes
components.summary: The controller indexes pose and request tables by the current reaction byte, then invokes additional reaction-specific handlers. Collision entry also dispatches on reaction, so a transformed form changes more than the avatar graphics.

components.label: Collision-triggered form changes
components.summary: Contact helpers request flaming, fat, zombie, snowman, puffy, bouncy, bat, frozen, flat and mask reactions. The shared macro checks WarioCheckReaction before changing the reaction and requesting pose zero; eligibility and recovery details are outside this extraction.

components.label: Motion history drives collision direction
components.summary: The collision wrapper compares current and previous X/Y positions to construct horizontal and vertical movement-direction flags. It then invokes reaction-indexed handlers; enumerated normal poses include jumping, rolling, crouching, swimming-related alternatives and ladders, without establishing their numeric acceleration values.

components.label: Damage-pose immunity gate
components.summary: Left and right damage helpers ignore contacts while damageTimer is positive. Otherwise they set a direction and request the taking-damage pose; the excerpt does not establish heart decrement amount or invulnerability duration.

components.label: Carryable rock state machine
components.summary: A rock can enter directional lifting and carried poses, with distinct helpers that position it relative to the actor. Carried initialization suppresses immediate actor collision and clears a death-related flag; ground pound selects a directional bump according to relative X.

components.label: Directional soft and hard throws
components.summary: The rock dispatches separate left/right and upward soft/hard projectile handlers. Hard throws store directional continuation bits in the high nibble of health, allowing a later collision pose to choose its next motion routine.

components.label: Return switch starts the escape phase
components.summary: The switch handler records persistent activation, sets gSwitchPressed and gTimerState to one, and changes the escape switch state. It resets the shared timer counter, spawns secondary effects and stops current music; the initial timer values are not established here.

components.label: Switch-gated return portal
components.summary: The vortex initially shrinks and becomes noninteractive; gSwitchPressed triggers an expansion phase before its idle state permits actor collision. The finish callback disables control, starts a stage-clear presentation and calls AutosaveStageClear.

components.label: Eligibility-gated deadline counter
components.summary: The escape updater advances only in active gameplay submode two, timer states zero through three and with no actor pause timer. When timer state is one, a 64-update cadence decrements decimal time digits; reaching zero changes timer state or enters failure depending on the remaining stage score.

components.label: Timeout spends score before terminal failure
components.summary: In post-countdown states above one, the updater subtracts one native score unit every eight eligible gameplay updates and emits a loss effect. A zero stage score changes timer state to four and starts the failure presentation; route planning and preserving a score reserve are inferred player strategies, not directly observed skill measurements.

components.label: Exit-associated token persists beyond its sprite
components.summary: Collecting Keyzer removes its sprite, marks the room slot despawned and sets gCollectedKeyzer. Reinitializing an already collected token suppresses respawn; stage-clear banking copies this flag into the persistent collection, while the exact stage-selection door predicate remains untraced.

components.label: Complete stage jewels announce boss-door opening
components.summary: Four directional jewel-piece flags are banked on stage clear. If a run flag has the special value two, the routine counts fully completed stage jewels and sets the boss-door presentation flag when all four ordinary stages, or the single entry/golden stage, are complete.

components.label: Four completed passage bosses unlock the final passage
components.summary: Boss clear banks the collected boss rewards and boss-defeated state. Defeating all four central passage bosses changes the current passage to Golden.

components.label: All final treasures unlock super-hard from hard
components.summary: Final-boss saving checks all twelve final treasure flags. A hard-difficulty clear with the complete treasure set changes the title style and clear message to announce super-hard; other combinations produce all-treasure or try-again messages.

components.label: Discrete score pickups
components.summary: Coins award 10, 50, 100, 500 or 1000 displayed points according to sprite ID. A diamond uses the 1000-point reward and remembers collection in room persistence, whereas small hearts feed a separate gauge.

components.label: Enemy-specific recoverable score scatter
components.summary: A damaging enemy identity chooses a requested score loss from 100 to 500 displayed points. ScoreGiveOrDropCoins emits coins at the actor position and subtracts at most the available stage score; recovery opportunities follow from the scattered pickups rather than an inferred fixed loss.

components.label: Queued heart refill with caps
components.summary: A full refill adds eight queued hearts, then clamps the queue so current plus filling cannot exceed eight. Little-heart pickups instead add one queued auxiliary gauge unit only while current plus filling remains below its eight-unit maximum; the conversion routine has not been decoded.

components.label: Bank collections and health bonus on successful exit
components.summary: Stage clear adds stage score plus fifty displayed points per remaining or queued heart to the total. The heart contribution is capped at eight, and saved high score and total score are capped at 999990 points; protecting health for the clear bonus is an inferred scoring strategy.

components.label: Persistent attack-opened reward container
components.summary: Opening a treasure box changes its room-persistent pose and starts a thirteen-frame transition. Completion emits a 500-point coin plus the relevant treasure child in its specific handler; already collected treasures are suppressed and the empty container disappears after its timer.

components.label: Terrain-probed directional patrol
components.summary: Yellow spear-mask movement samples support and adjacent terrain before selecting falling, turning or walking. Its walking helper uses three native subpixels per update normally and one or two for specific terrain-code values; mapping these codes to named slope types remains unverified.

components.label: Facing and proximity-gated red-enemy chase
components.summary: A red spear mask in idle begins a chase when the actor lies within a forward-facing horizontal neighborhood and a narrow vertical band. A twenty-four-frame preparation precedes chasing, whose helper increases the normal movement step from 0.75 to 1 pixel per update; baiting or avoiding that range is a strategy inferred from the state machine.

components.label: Boss timer and presentation initialization
components.summary: Boss initiation requests standing, pauses actor control for two hundred frames and activates timer state one. It resets the shared timer counter and chooses final-boss or regular-boss music by passage; this establishes initialization, not a boss damage or attack model.

components.label: Duration-prioritized screen shake
components.summary: A nonzero request replaces an axis only if its duration exceeds the remaining duration. Updates insert zero-offset frames and alternating offsets, reducing the magnitude near the end; the amplitude field behaves as a flag/sign input rather than an arbitrary pixel multiplier in this implementation.

components.label: Subpixel layer scroll converted to hardware offsets
components.summary: The scroll routine divides layer positions by four before masking offsets to nine bits and adding shake. BG3 receives half the vertical shake while other layers use the full offset; the complete camera follow/clamp policy is not established by this register-preparation routine.

components.label: Planar side-view sprite presentation
components.summary: Actor rendering subtracts camera X/Y from world X/Y, converts to pixels and adds OAM-piece offsets. The inspected platform scene shows side-on rooms, horizontal platforms and vertical traversal; no perspective depth calculation appears in this draw path.

components.label: Buffered sprites and animation tiles transferred during VBlank
components.summary: The gameplay VBlank callback copies OAM with DMA3, streams up to two actor graphics blocks, copies actor palettes and uploads health/gauge tiles. This is a concrete asset-to-display path; asset semantic labels and complete palette inventories remain unextracted.

components.label: Rotating and scaling multipart vortex sprite
components.summary: A vortex creates child sprite parts and updates four affine coefficients from sine, cosine and inverse scale. Scale and angle are presentation state, while the portal collision gate is handled separately by pose.

components.label: Tile and water-driven alpha targets
components.summary: Tile metadata under the actor selects a target alpha from a small table or default, then the current alpha moves by one step toward it. A water-related variant also selects sounds when its alpha target changes; these are material/context responses, not evidence of global per-scanline effects.

components.label: Measured boot/front-end display mode changes
components.summary: The retained 9000-frame capture recorded mode zero for 7664 frames, mode one for 480, and mode four for 806. Affine background/object, alpha blend, brightness and window flags were observed, but these phase-aggregated measurements do not prove each effect occurs during active gameplay.

components.label: Measured PCM and PSG activity
components.summary: The capture records both DirectSound channels with a reported 13379 Hz timer rate and PSG activity on channels one, two and four. These are capture-observed channel statistics rather than a claim about every composition or gameplay state.

components.label: Underwater variants of pickup feedback
components.summary: Coin and diamond collection choose different sound IDs when the reaction equals water. Keyzer has the same context branch, making state-dependent auditory feedback explicit without inferring its exact acoustic processing.

components.label: Random event voice sets protect current speech
components.summary: A voice event chooses an entry using MinigameRandom modulo the selected set size. Most voice sets return early while the voice player is active; hurry-up is excluded from that protection and may interrupt.

components.label: A staged visual prologue before playable platforming
components.summary: The viewed attract frame depicts a small dark cat, crescent moon and masonry silhouette, without a gameplay HUD. Main mode routing identifies a cutscene subsystem separate from demos and active play; the complete plot and scene ordering were not established.

components.label: Moonlit masonry and colorful treasure-platform spaces
components.summary: The inspected intro depicts moonlit dark masonry, while the inspected gameplay scene uses saturated purple and green stone platforms, a door-like object and colorful characters. This records visible environmental motifs, without inferring named locations, factions or story causality.

identity.tagline: A treasure hunt turns into a frantic return trip when the exit switch is hit.
